XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Last weekend, on BBC Politics Wales, you said you were, quote, 'quite shocked' by the financial pressures facing the Welsh Government and the reality of the Welsh budget when you came into the role of finance Minister. So, Minister, what specifically about the state of the Welsh finances came as a surprise to you after taking office?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Y penwythnos diwethaf, ar Politics Wales y BBC, fe ddywedoch chi eich bod wedi cael tipyn o sioc o weld y pwysau ariannol sy'n wynebu Llywodraeth Cymru a realiti cyllideb Cymru pan ddaethoch i rôl y Gweinidog cyllid. Felly, Weinidog, beth yn benodol am gyflwr cyllid Cymru oedd yn syndod i chi ar ôl i chi ddechrau yn eich swydd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: There are two aspects to this; I've spoken, actually, twice on the politics show on both of them. One was the in-year challenges that the Welsh Government inherited as a result of the budget that was laid last year and passed last year. The pressures in particular from within the NHS are considerable, and they were considerably more than I expected them to be. They are a challenge within the financial year that I'm trying to manage as we speak. But also, in a world where—and we've heard it again today—the inflationary pressures in our wider society and economy mean that the budget next year, at the moment, is 0.7 per cent less in real terms, that is very challenging in the context of the wage inflation that is within our public services as well. So, those were two aspects that were particularly challenging for public services in Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae dwy elfen i hyn; rwyf wedi siarad am y ddwy, ddwywaith mewn gwirionedd, ar y rhaglen wleidyddiaeth. Un oedd yr heriau yn ystod y flwyddyn a etifeddodd Llywodraeth Cymru o ganlyniad i'r gyllideb a osodwyd y llynedd ac a basiwyd y llynedd. Mae'r pwysau yn enwedig o fewn y GIG yn sylweddol, ac roedd yn llawer mwy na'r hyn y disgwyliwn iddo fod. Mae'n her o fewn y flwyddyn ariannol yr wyf yn ceisio'i rheoli wrth inni siarad. Ond hefyd, mewn byd lle mae'r pwysau chwyddiant—ac rydym wedi ei glywed eto heddiw—yn ein cymdeithas a'n heconomi ehangach yn golygu bod y gyllideb y flwyddyn nesaf, ar hyn o bryd, 0.7 y cant yn llai mewn termau real, mae hynny'n heriol iawn yng nghyd-destun y chwyddiant cyflogau yn ein gwasanaethau cyhoeddus hefyd. Felly, roedd y rhain yn ddwy elfen a oedd yn arbennig o heriol i wasanaethau cyhoeddus yng Nghymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I don't understand how that was a shock when you became finance Minister, because it was already known that there would be a reduction, unless you just didn't do your research before becoming finance Minister.

Anyway, Plaid Cymru went into the Senedd election saying that their manifesto was fully costed. Given these shocks you now have, can you confirm to us that your manifesto would not be labelled 'fully costed' if you had the information you have today?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Nid wyf yn deall sut roedd hynny'n sioc pan ddaethoch yn Weinidog cyllid, oherwydd roedd eisoes yn hysbys y byddai gostyngiad, oni bai eich bod heb wneud eich ymchwil cyn dod yn Weinidog cyllid.

Beth bynnag, aeth Plaid Cymru i mewn i etholiad y Senedd gan ddweud bod eu maniffesto wedi ei gostio'n llawn. O ystyried y siociau hyn sydd gennych bellach, a allwch chi gadarnhau i ni na fyddai eich maniffesto wedi cael ei labelu fel un wedi ei gostio'n llawn pe bai gennych yr wybodaeth sydd gennych heddiw?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
It was fully costed, but the job of work that we have to do as a Government, and I've alluded to it already, is the discipline now that Ministers have to face in allocating within their priorities how they marry the priorities that a governing party brings into Government with the day-to-day running of public services. 

I spoke of the three components of the budget as I see them: the effective running of public services in Wales and how we fund those in the budget settlement that we have as a Senedd and Government; and then the priorities that the Plaid Cymru Government, as voted for by the people of Wales, bring into that; as well as then, of course, the ability that other political parties will want to influence that budget as a third component part of it. So, putting all of that together in one blended melting pot is what we're doing as we speak. Doing that at a time of more financial flexibility would have made it an easier and more constructive piece of work to undertake. It is going to be a challenging piece of work. As I've hopefully set out today, I hope that we're all up for that challenge as a Senedd together.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Roedd wedi ei gostio'n llawn, ond y gwaith y mae'n rhaid inni ei wneud fel Llywodraeth, ac rwyf wedi cyfeirio ato eisoes, yw'r ddisgyblaeth y mae'n rhaid i Weinidogion ei hwynebu nawr wrth ddyrannu o fewn eu blaenoriaethau sut y maent yn cyfuno'r blaenoriaethau y mae plaid lywodraethol yn eu dwyn i'r Llywodraeth gyda rhedeg gwasanaethau cyhoeddus o ddydd i ddydd. 

Siaradais am dair elfen y gyllideb fel y'u gwelaf: rhedeg gwasanaethau cyhoeddus yng Nghymru yn effeithiol a sut rydym yn ariannu'r rheini yn y setliad cyllidebol a gawn fel Senedd a Llywodraeth; ac yna'r blaenoriaethau y mae Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru, fel y pleidleisiwyd drosti gan bobl Cymru, yn eu dwyn i mewn i hynny; yn ogystal wedyn, wrth gwrs, â'r gallu i bleidiau gwleidyddol eraill ddylanwadu ar y gyllideb honno fel trydedd elfen. Felly, rhoi hynny i gyd at ei gilydd mewn un pair cyfunol yw'r hyn rydym yn ei wneud wrth inni siarad. Byddai gwneud hynny ar adeg o fwy o hyblygrwydd ariannol wedi ei wneud yn waith haws a mwy adeiladol. Mae'n mynd i fod yn waith heriol. Fel y nodais heddiw, rwy'n gobeithio ein bod i gyd yn barod am yr her honno fel Senedd gyda'n gilydd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. You've spoken about cuts, but not taxes. However, actions speak louder than words. From April, the Welsh Government has introduced a higher business rates multiplier for larger premises. Is this the direction that you think this Government is going to go towards in dealing with the financial issues? Are you considering other tax rises, including income tax?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Rydych chi wedi siarad am doriadau, ond nid trethi. Fodd bynnag, mae gweithredoedd yn golygu mwy na geiriau. O fis Ebrill, mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi cyflwyno lluosydd ardrethi busnes uwch ar gyfer safleoedd mwy o faint. Ai dyma'r cyfeiriad y credwch y bydd y Llywodraeth hon yn mynd iddo wrth ymdrin â'r materion ariannol? A ydych chi'n ystyried codiadau treth eraill, gan gynnwys treth incwm?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I accept that there is a higher ask of those businesses across the business rates portfolio that have the higher rateable values. The bit you didn't mention in your question was those up to 20,000 businesses that will benefit from lower taxes as a result of the announcement yesterday and the support for retail premises as well. I think the premise of your question is, though, that this is not just about how we allocate the public funding that's available to us, but how we also use our taxation system to ensure, yes, that we're using it to fund public services, because taxation is what enables public services to be run, but also how we get that balance right in terms of supporting our economy. All of those together, again, are part of the considerations when we need to think about where we strike this balance.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n derbyn bod y gofyn yn uwch i'r busnesau ar draws y portffolio ardrethi busnes sydd â'r gwerthoedd ardrethol uwch. Y peth na sonioch chi amdano yn eich cwestiwn oedd yr hyd at 20,000 o fusnesau a fydd yn elwa o drethi is o ganlyniad i'r cyhoeddiad ddoe a'r cymorth i safleoedd manwerthu yn ogystal. Rwy'n credu mai cynsail eich cwestiwn, fodd bynnag, yw bod hyn nid yn unig yn ymwneud â sut rydym yn dyrannu'r cyllid cyhoeddus sydd ar gael inni, ond sut rydym ni hefyd yn defnyddio ein system drethi i sicrhau, ie, ein bod yn ei defnyddio i ariannu gwasanaethau cyhoeddus, oherwydd trethiant yw'r hyn sy'n galluogi i wasanaethau cyhoeddus gael eu rhedeg, ond hefyd sut y cawn y cydbwysedd hwnnw'n iawn er mwyn cefnogi ein heconomi. Mae pob un ohonynt gyda'i gilydd, unwaith eto, yn rhan o'r ystyriaethau pan fydd angen inni feddwl ble i daro'r cydbwysedd hwn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd Llafur Cymru, Huw Thomas.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Welsh Labour spokesperson, Huw Thomas.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Mae arnaf i ofn fod Cai Parry-Jones wedi bod yn copïo fy ngwaith cartref i, achos roeddwn i hefyd yn mynd i'ch holi chi am eich sylwadau chi ar Politics Wales. Roedd hi'n syndod i fi hefyd glywed am y sioc roeddech chi'n ei theimlo o ran y pwysau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wynebu.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, Dirprwy Lywydd. I'm afraid that Cai Parry-Jones has been copying my homework, because I too was going to ask about your comments on Politics Wales. It came as a surprise to me too to hear of your shock in looking at the pressures facing the Welsh Government.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cai has made reference to some of the commentary around the pressures facing Welsh Government in its next budget. The IFS, the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned in the election campaign about the extremely challenging fiscal outlook facing the next Government, and yet your own party leader assured voters that Plaid Cymru had a fully costed programme for government. It does start to feel now like these were simply making promises without preparing for the consequences. I don't want to repeat Cai's question, so let me ask, therefore: if the Government faces a choice between funding its manifesto promises or making cuts to core public services and projects, how will it decide?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae Cai wedi cyfeirio at rai o'r sylwadau ynghylch y pwysau sy'n wynebu Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei chyllideb nesaf. Rhybuddiodd y Sefydliad Astudiaethau Cyllidol yn yr ymgyrch etholiadol am y rhagolygon cyllidol hynod heriol oedd yn wynebu'r Llywodraeth nesaf, ac eto mae arweinydd eich plaid eich hun wedi sicrhau pleidleiswyr fod gan Blaid Cymru raglen lywodraethu wedi'i chostio'n llawn. Mae'n dechrau teimlo bellach fel pe bai'r rhain yn addewidion a wnaed heb baratoi ar gyfer y canlyniadau. Nid wyf am ailadrodd cwestiwn Cai, felly gadewch imi ofyn, felly: os yw'r Llywodraeth yn wynebu dewis rhwng ariannu ei haddewidion maniffesto neu wneud toriadau i wasanaethau cyhoeddus a phrosiectau craidd, sut y bydd yn penderfynu?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Dwi'n meddwl bod y cwestiwn yna yn un gwirioneddol ddiddorol, ac yn wirioneddol yn gwestiwn sydd yn ein hwynebu ni fel Llywodraeth, sy'n Llywodraeth am y tro cyntaf. Rydym ni wedi etifeddu cyllidebau sydd wedi cael eu cynllunio gan bleidiau eraill a Llywodraethau o'n blaenau ni, er ein bod ni fel plaid hefyd wedi cefnogi agweddau o'r cyllidebau hynny. Mae'n wir i ddweud ein bod ni fel Llywodraeth a Gweinidogion y Llywodraeth yma yn edrych ar draws holl gyllidebau'r Llywodraeth ar hyn o bryd i weld beth sydd yn gweithio'n effeithiol, beth sydd angen ei newid, a lle mae toriadau. Gyda llaw, byddwch chi'n dod i wybod hyn, dwi ddim yn Weinidog cyllid sy'n ofni defnyddio'r gair 'toriadau'. Mewn rhai llefydd, mae toriadau yn beth da. Mewn llefydd eraill, dydyn nhw ddim. Ond dwi ddim yn mynd i osgoi defnyddio'r term.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I think that that question is a truly interesting one, and is truly a question that faces us as a Government, who are in Government for the first time. We've inherited budgets that have been planned by other parties and previous Governments, although we as a party did support aspects of those budgets. It is true to say that we as a Government and Ministers within that Government are looking across all the Government budgets at present to see what's working effectively, what needs to change, and where there are cuts. By the way, you'll get to know this, I'm not a Minister for finance who is afraid to use the word 'cuts'. In some places, cuts are a good thing. In other places, they're not. But I'm not going to avoid using that term.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'm not going to be one of those Ministers who avoids the term 'cuts' at all times and tries to say 'efficiencies' or other ways of describing it.

So, all of these factors are in the melting pot, as I see it, at this time. That overview of the whole budget of Government is currently a disciplined process that the Ministers are looking at, so that we reprioritise spend in terms of some of the priorities that Plaid Cymru has brought in to Government, but also that we look to see which budget areas are properly delivering the outcomes that another Member spoke of earlier. Because we really have to look at where the outcomes are best achieved, rather than just looking at headings on budget lines at all times.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Nid wyf am fod yn un o'r Gweinidogion hynny sy'n osgoi'r term 'toriadau' bob amser ac sy'n ceisio dweud 'arbedion effeithlonrwydd' neu ffyrdd eraill o'i ddisgrifio.

Felly, mae'r holl ffactorau hyn yn y pair, fel y'i gwelaf, ar hyn o bryd. Mae'r trosolwg hwnnw o gyllideb gyfan y Llywodraeth ar hyn o bryd yn broses ddisgybledig y mae'r Gweinidogion yn edrych arni, fel ein bod yn ail-flaenoriaethu gwariant yn nhermau rhai o'r blaenoriaethau y mae Plaid Cymru wedi'u dwyn i mewn i Lywodraeth, ond hefyd ein bod yn edrych i weld pa feysydd cyllideb sy'n cyflawni'n briodol y canlyniadau y soniodd Aelod arall amdanynt yn gynharach. Oherwydd mae'n rhaid inni edrych ar ble mae'r canlyniadau'n cael eu cyflawni orau, yn hytrach nag edrych yn unig ar benawdau llinellau cyllideb bob amser.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Weinidog. I'm sure you would concede that difficult budget decisions and cuts are rarely felt equally. Women, disabled people, minority ethnic communities, children and those already experiencing poverty are often placed most at risk when public spending is constrained. Under the previous Welsh Labour Government, there was the budget improvement and impact advisory group, bringing organisations representing those communities directly into the budget-setting process. We've now been told by equality stakeholders that the group has not met under this Plaid Cymru Welsh Government and they've had no assurance about its future.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog. Rwy'n siŵr y byddech chi'n cyfaddef mai anaml y teimlir penderfyniadau a thoriadau cyllidebol anodd yn gyfartal. Yn aml, menywod, pobl anabl, cymunedau ethnig leiafrifol, plant a'r rhai sydd eisoes yn profi tlodi sy'n wynebu'r risg fwyaf pan gyfyngir ar wariant cyhoeddus. O dan y Llywodraeth Llafur Cymru flaenorol, roedd yna grŵp cynghori ar wella ac asesu effaith y gyllideb, gan ddod â sefydliadau sy'n cynrychioli'r cymunedau hynny i mewn yn uniongyrchol i'r broses o osod y gyllideb. Mae rhanddeiliaid cydraddoldeb bellach wedi dweud wrthym nad yw'r grŵp wedi cyfarfod o dan Lywodraeth Plaid Cymru ac nad ydynt wedi cael unrhyw sicrwydd ynghylch ei ddyfodol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: A wnewch chi ymrwymo, Weinidog, i ailsefydlu'r grŵp yma a chomitio i ymgysylltu ystyrlon â mudiadau cydraddoldeb wrth gynllunio'r gyllideb, ac nid i simply ymgynghori ar ôl i'r penderfyniadau mawr gael eu gwneud?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Will you commit, Minister, to re-establish this group and also commit to meaningful engagement with equalities organisations when planning your budget, and not to simply consult once the major decisions have been made?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Dwi yn fodlon ymrwymo i edrych ar y mater yma. Dyw e ddim yn fater dwi'n hollol gyfarwydd ag e. Dwi yn gweld y gwerth sydd yna a dwi'n ymwybodol iawn bod fy nghyd-Weinidogion yn ymwybodol iawn bod impact unrhyw newidiadau cyllid angen cael eu hasesu ac angen mynd drwy'r lens yna rŷch chi'n sôn amdano. Dŷn ni ddim eisiau gweld taw'r bobl fwyaf difreintiedig neu anghenus fydd yn dioddef o unrhyw newidiadau i'r gyllideb. Felly, mae hwnna'n rhywbeth rŷn ni'n mynd i eisiau iddo fod yn ffactor allweddol yn sut rŷn ni'n gwneud yr asesiadau cyllidol yma. Ac felly, mi wnaf i edrych yn benodol ar y grŵp rŷch chi newydd sôn amdano i weld sut gallwn ni fod yn dwyn y drafodaeth yn ei blaen gyda'r arbenigwyr yna.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I am willing to commit to look at this issue. It's not an issue that I'm completely familiar with. I do see the value in it and I am aware that my fellow Ministers are very aware that the impact of any budgetary changes need to be assessed and need to be viewed through that lens you're talking about. We don't want to see the most disadvantaged or needy people suffering as a result of any budgetary changes. So, that's something we want to regard as a key factor in terms of how we undertake these budgetary assessments. So, I'll look specifically at the group that you just mentioned to see how we can progress that discussion with those experts.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig, Sam Rowlands.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Welsh Conservatives spokesperson, Sam Rowlands.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Deputy Presiding Officer. Cabinet Minister, how do you ensure that taxpayers' money is not wasted?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Weinidog Cabinet, sut rydych chi'n sicrhau nad yw arian trethdalwyr yn cael ei wastraffu?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, I think, by doing the job of work that I outlined just earlier. We're a new Government, we have a new lens and, hopefully, a new energy into wanting to make the best use of the Welsh pound and to make sure that we are outcomes led in how we take our financial decisions. I recognise that we have a particular opportunity to do that in our first annual budget, and therefore there is considerable impetus from me, and from my Cabinet colleague on effectiveness of Government delivery, to be looking at how we ensure that the budgets that we will put to this Senedd are as outcomes focused as they can be and, as I've spoken of already, that they're not just lines on a spreadsheet, but they're actually meaningful in terms of what they will be delivering.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, trwy wneud y gwaith a amlinellais yn gynharach. Rydym yn Llywodraeth newydd, mae gennym lens newydd, ac egni newydd, gobeithio, i fod eisiau gwneud y defnydd gorau o'r bunt Gymreig ac i wneud yn siŵr ein bod yn cael ein harwain gan ganlyniadau yn y ffordd y gwnawn ein penderfyniadau ariannol. Rwy'n cydnabod bod gennym gyfle arbennig i wneud hynny yn ein cyllideb flynyddol gyntaf, ac felly mae ysgogiad sylweddol gennyf i, a chan fy nghyd-Aelod yn y Cabinet ar effeithlonrwydd cyflawniad y Llywodraeth, i edrych ar sut rydym yn sicrhau bod y cyllidebau y byddwn yn eu rhoi gerbron y Senedd hon yn canolbwyntio cymaint ag y gallant ar ganlyniadau, ac fel y nodais eisoes, nad ydynt yn llinellau ar daenlen yn unig, ond eu bod yn ystyrlon o ran yr hyn y byddant yn ei gyflawni.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, thank you for your response, Cabinet Minister. Last week, the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy released a written statement informing Members that the Welsh Government is going to write off £684,000 in unpaid rent owed by P.V. France Limited, a significant amount of taxpayers' money. There may be some specific reasons why that business went into difficulty, but what concerns me is how that debt of nearly £700,000 was allowed to reach such an extraordinary level in the first place. The Welsh Government, we understand, agreed to multiple payment plans, yet the arrears continued to build time after time. The company eventually entered administration, was dissolved, and now that money, nearly £700,000, seemingly cannot be recovered. 

At a time when we're being told that the public finances are incredibly tight, as I'm sure they are, how can the Government justify allowing almost £700,000 of taxpayers' money to be lost in this way? And as the Minister responsible for holding those purse strings, how will you prevent this from happening again in the future?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wel, diolch am eich ymateb, Weinidog Cabinet. Yr wythnos diwethaf, rhyddhaodd y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni ddatganiad ysgrifenedig yn hysbysu'r Aelodau fod Llywodraeth Cymru yn mynd i ddileu £684,000 o rent heb ei dalu sy'n ddyledus gan P.V. France Limited, swm sylweddol o arian trethdalwyr. Efallai fod rhesymau penodol pam yr aeth y busnes hwnnw i drafferthion, ond yr hyn sy'n fy mhoeni i yw sut y caniatawyd i'r ddyled honno o bron i £700,000 gyrraedd lefel mor eithriadol o uchel yn y lle cyntaf. Deallwn fod Llywodraeth Cymru wedi cytuno i sawl cynllun talu, ond parhaodd yr ôl-ddyledion i gynyddu dro ar ôl tro. Yn y pen draw, aeth y cwmni i ddwylo'r gweinyddwyr, cafodd ei ddiddymu, ac erbyn hyn mae'n debyg na ellir adennill yr arian hwnnw, bron i £700,000.

Ar adeg pan ddywedwyd wrthym fod y cyllid cyhoeddus yn anhygoel o dynn, ac rwy'n siŵr ei fod, sut y gall y Llywodraeth gyfiawnhau caniatáu i bron i £700,000 o arian trethdalwyr gael ei golli yn y modd hwn? Ac fel y Gweinidog sy'n gyfrifol am ddal llinynnau'r pwrs, sut y byddwch chi'n atal hyn rhag digwydd eto yn y dyfodol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, it concerns me too that that level of debt was allowed to accrue without the Government being able to monitor it in an effective way, and I'm aware from cases in the past, not particularly this one, that this can happen. Government is always about investing properly in economic development and in running public services. Sometimes, that investment needs to happen in a context where there is risk, and Ministers need to balance that risk. But making sure that we have the right financial controls in place in a risky situation or not—. We need to make sure that those financial control measures are in place, because £700,000 is, as you could describe, or I could describe, money that would have been better spent elsewhere.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, mae'n fy mhoeni innau hefyd fod y lefel honno o ddyled wedi cael ei gadael i gronni heb i'r Llywodraeth allu ei monitro mewn ffordd effeithiol, ac rwy'n ymwybodol o achosion yn y gorffennol, nid yr un hwn yn benodol, y gall hyn ddigwydd. Mae a wnelo Llywodraeth bob amser â buddsoddi'n briodol mewn datblygiad economaidd ac mewn rhedeg gwasanaethau cyhoeddus. Weithiau, mae angen i'r buddsoddiad hwnnw ddigwydd mewn cyd-destun lle mae risg, ac mae angen i Weinidogion gydbwyso'r risg honno. Ond mae gwneud yn siŵr bod gennym y mesurau rheoli ariannol cywir ar waith mewn sefyllfa o risg neu beidio—. Mae angen inni wneud yn siŵr bod y mesurau rheoli ariannol hynny ar waith, oherwydd mae £700,000, fel y gallech chi ei ddisgrifio, neu y gallwn i ei ddisgrifio, yn arian a fyddai wedi cael ei wario'n well mewn mannau eraill.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Polisi Cyllid Llywodraeth Leol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Local Government Finance Policy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 3. A wnaiff y Gweinidog Cabinet nodi blaenoriaethau Llywodraeth Cymru o ran polisi cyllid llywodraeth leol yn ystod y Senedd hon? OQ64434
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 3. Will the Cabinet Minister set out the Welsh Government’s priorities regarding local government finance policy during this Senedd? OQ64434

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. O fewn Llywodraeth Cymru, mae'r cyfrifoldeb am lywodraeth leol yn dod o dan fy nghydweithiwr, y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio. Gan weithio gyda llywodraeth leol, rŷn ni wedi cyflawni ein hymrwymiad 100-diwrnod i gomisiynu adolygiad o fformiwla gyllido llywodraeth leol.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you. Within the Welsh Government, responsibility for local government lies with my colleague the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning. Working with local government, we have delivered our 100-day commitment to commission a review of the local government funding formula.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for that answer, Cabinet Minister. In the wake of the announcement that the Welsh Government was going to review the local government funding formula, I know that you and the local government Minister received a letter from the leader of Merthyr Tydfil County Borough Council, and this firmly made the case that any review should not have a detrimental impact upon that council or the residents and communities that it serves. So, Cabinet Minister, I'm seeking similar assurances today that any review won't negatively affect either Merthyr Tydfil council or Rhondda Cynon Taf County Borough Council in view of the demographic challenges specifically that they face, and also that all councils will be fully involved in the process as it develops.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am yr ateb hwnnw, Weinidog Cabinet. Yn sgil y cyhoeddiad fod Llywodraeth Cymru yn mynd i adolygu fformiwla ariannu llywodraeth leol, gwn eich bod chi a'r Gweinidog llywodraeth leol wedi cael llythyr gan arweinydd Cyngor Bwrdeistref Sirol Merthyr Tudful, ac roedd yn dadlau'n gadarn na ddylai unrhyw adolygiad gael effaith niweidiol ar y cyngor hwnnw na'r trigolion a'r cymunedau y mae'n eu gwasanaethu. Felly, Weinidog Cabinet, rwy'n ceisio sicrwydd tebyg heddiw na fydd unrhyw adolygiad yn effeithio'n negyddol ar gyngor Merthyr Tudful na Chyngor Bwrdeistref Sirol Rhondda Cynon Taf yng ngoleuni'r heriau demograffig penodol y maent yn eu hwynebu, a hefyd y bydd pob cyngor yn cymryd rhan lawn yn y broses wrth iddi ddatblygu.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Yes, I can certainly give you the complete confidence that local government is a key partner in the work that we're doing on this review through its existing mechanisms, so that we do look properly at all aspects of work that need to feature in a review of this nature. And that does reflect on, and needs to reflect on, the patterns of need that we have throughout our communities and also the costs of delivering services across communities as well. So, it is a joint piece of work. I see it as a joint piece of work with local government. We want to be, as you were previously, a Government in partnership—working in partnership with local government. They are key to the delivery of public services in Wales. They're not key to it, they do it—they do the delivery of public services in Wales, and we need to make sure that they are funded in a way that enables that work to happen as effectively as possible in every community in Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Gallaf yn sicr roi hyder llwyr i chi fod llywodraeth leol yn bartner allweddol yn y gwaith a wnawn ar yr adolygiad hwn trwy ei fecanweithiau presennol, fel ein bod yn edrych yn iawn ar bob agwedd ar y gwaith y mae angen ei wneud mewn adolygiad o'r natur hon. Ac mae hynny'n ystyried, ac mae angen iddo ystyried, y patrymau angen sydd gennym ledled ein cymunedau a hefyd y costau o ddarparu gwasanaethau ar draws cymunedau. Felly, mae'n waith ar y cyd. Rwy'n ei weld fel gwaith ar y cyd â llywodraeth leol. Rydym am fod, fel roeddech chi'n flaenorol, yn Llywodraeth mewn partneriaeth—gan weithio mewn partneriaeth â llywodraeth leol. Maent yn allweddol i ddarparu gwasanaethau cyhoeddus yng Nghymru. Nid ydynt yn allweddol iddo, maent yn ei wneud—maent yn darparu gwasanaethau cyhoeddus yng Nghymru, ac mae angen inni wneud yn siŵr eu bod yn cael eu hariannu mewn ffordd sy'n ei gwneud hi'n bosibl i'r gwaith hwnnw ddigwydd mor effeithiol â phosibl ym mhob cymuned yng Nghymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, Plaid's inability to pass the budget has left councils in limbo. Local authorities needs as much time as possible to budget for the upcoming financial year. Audit Wales said that the Welsh Government's handling of restricted grants makes it hard for councils to plan. Audit Wales also found that £1.5 billion was allocated to councils in March 2025—the final month of the 2024-25 financial year. That represents 20 per cent of the annual total of this funding grant. So, Minister, what is the Welsh Government doing to give councils more certainty when setting their budgets, instead of leaving it to the last minute?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, mae anallu Plaid Cymru i basio'r gyllideb wedi achosi ansicrwydd i gynghorau. Mae angen cymaint o amser â phosibl ar awdurdodau lleol i gyllidebu ar gyfer y flwyddyn ariannol sydd i ddod. Dywedodd Archwilio Cymru fod y ffordd y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ymdrin â grantiau cyfyngedig yn ei gwneud yn anodd i gynghorau gynllunio. Canfu Archwilio Cymru hefyd fod £1.5 biliwn wedi'i ddyrannu i gynghorau ym mis Mawrth 2025—mis olaf blwyddyn ariannol 2024-25. Mae hynny'n 20 y cant o gyfanswm blynyddol y grant cyllid hwn. Felly, Weinidog, beth y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud i roi mwy o sicrwydd i gynghorau wrth iddynt osod eu cyllidebau, yn hytrach na'i adael tan y funud olaf?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I agree 100 per cent with the need for us to be able to present a budget and to pass a budget in this place in as early as possible a way in order to provide that security and that lead-in time for planning and effective delivery of services by local authorities. We have a UK Government budget that happens at the end of October, and we are hoping to be able to pass a Senedd budget in the early part of January or February next year. I'm not going to miss the opportunity to say that the best way of giving certainty to local authorities, NHS, public services, public bodies, businesses in Wales, is that we can find a way of ensuring that a budget in this place has a majority to enable it to pass. Anything that stifles that process over the next few weeks and months will ultimately end in local authorities in Wales not having the ability to pass their own budgets in time.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n cytuno 100 y cant â'r angen inni allu cyflwyno cyllideb ac i basio cyllideb yn y lle hwn cyn gynted â phosibl er mwyn darparu'r diogelwch hwnnw a'r amser rhagarweiniol hwnnw ar gyfer cynllunio a darparu gwasanaethau effeithiol gan awdurdodau lleol. Mae gennym gyllideb Llywodraeth y DU sy'n digwydd ddiwedd mis Hydref, ac rydym yn gobeithio gallu pasio cyllideb y Senedd ddechrau mis Ionawr neu fis Chwefror y flwyddyn nesaf. Nid wyf yn mynd i golli'r cyfle i ddweud mai'r ffordd orau o roi sicrwydd i awdurdodau lleol, y GIG, gwasanaethau cyhoeddus, cyrff cyhoeddus, busnesau yng Nghymru, yw gallu dod o hyd i ffordd o sicrhau bod gan gyllideb yn y lle hwn fwyafrif i'w gwneud hi'n bosibl ei phasio. Yn y pen draw, bydd unrhyw beth sy'n llesteirio'r broses honno dros yr wythnosau a'r misoedd nesaf yn golygu na fydd awdurdodau lleol yng Nghymru yn gallu pasio eu cyllidebau eu hunain mewn pryd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch i'r Aelod am ofyn y cwestiwn. Mae'r llu o grantiau bach sy'n cael eu dyrannu i awdurdodau lleol o flwyddyn i flwyddyn yn creu heriau gwirioneddol o ran cynllunio ymlaen llaw. Trwy ddiwygio'r grant cynnal refeniw i'w wneud yn decach ac yn fwy tryloyw, gellid sicrhau bod mwy o arian yn cyrraedd gwasanaethau rheng flaen. Nawr, dwi'n siŵr nad yw'r Gweinidog eisiau rhagdybio unrhyw adolygiad, ond ydy'r Gweinidog yn meddwl, drwy symleiddio'r ffordd y caiff llywodraeth leol ei hariannu, y gallai hynny wella'r sefyllfa bresennol?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I thank the Member for asking the question. The numerous small grants that are allocated to local authorities from year to year create real challenges in terms of advanced planning. By reforming the revenue support grant to make it fairer and more transparent, we can ensure that more money reaches front-line services. Now, I'm sure the Minister doesn't want to make any assumptions about any review, but does the Minister believe that simplifying the way that local government is funded could improve the current situation?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Ie, dwi'n meddwl bod y pwyntiau yna'n sicr o werth i awdurdodau lleol wrth iddyn nhw feddwl amboutu ariannu'r cynlluniau yna a'r gwasnaethau yna y maen nhw'n eu delifro. Ac felly, y lens yna rŷn ni'n moyn ei roi ar siẁd mae'r setliad ar gyfer llywodraeth leol yn gweithio'n fwy effeithiol, ond hefyd siẁd mae'r model o ariannu yn fwy cynhwysfawr yn gweithio hefyd. 

Mae rhoi'r rhyddid yna i lywodraeth leol i fedru penderfynu ar eu blaenoriaethau nhw eu hunain yn bart o ddatganoli o fewn Cymru, wrth gwrs, ac felly, os ydyn ni'n gallu cyflawni yr hyn rŷn ni eisiau trwy rymuso llywodraeth leol i fod yn arwain ar siẁd mae datblygu a chyflenwi gwasanaethau yn eu hardaloedd nhw, yna, fel Llywodraeth, byddwn ni'n falch iawn i glywed am syniadau sy'n dod wrth lywodraeth leol, ac yn dod o'r Senedd yma, fel y gallwn ni sicrhau bod y pecyn mwyaf effeithiol o ariannu yn cyrraedd llywodraeth leol, achos, fel dwi wedi dweud eisoes, nhw sy'n delifro gwasanaethau, ac maen nhw angen yr arfau hynny a'r pwerau hynny i fedru gwneud hynny'n effeithiol.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Well, yes, I think those points are valuable for local authorities as they think about funding those programmes and services that they deliver. And it's that lens that we want to apply as to how the local government settlement could work more effectively, but also how the funding model could work more comprehensively too.

Providing that freedom to local government to decide on their own priorities is part of devolution within Wales of course, and, therefore, if we can deliver what we want to achieve by empowering local government to lead on how to develop and deliver services in their own areas, then we as a Government would be very pleased to hear of any ideas coming from local government, and coming from this Senedd, of course, so that we can ensure that the most effective package of funding is provided to local government, because, as I've said already, they deliver services, and they need those tools and those powers to do that effectively.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Tanau Gwyllt Diweddar
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Recent Wildfires

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 4. Sut mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet yn gweithio gyda chydweithwyr y Cabinet i ddarparu cymorth ariannol i gominwyr a phobl eraill sydd wedi'u heffeithio gan y tanau gwyllt diweddar? OQ64453
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 4. How is the Cabinet Minister working with Cabinet colleagues to provide financial support to commoners and other people affected by the recent wildfires? OQ64453

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Dwi'n ymwybodol o effeithiau helaeth y tanau gwyllt ar ffermwyr a commoners hefyd. Os yn briodol, byddwn yn caniatáu eithriadau i ofynion cynllunio er mwyn helpu ffermwyr sydd wedi eu heffeithio. Mae ystyriaeth bellach yn cael ei roi hefyd i sut i gefnogi gwydnwch y sector yn wyneb pwysau sylweddol yr haf hwn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I'm aware of the extensive impacts of the wildfires on commoners and farmers. And if appropriate, we will allow exemptions to planning conditions in order to help farmers that have been affected. Further consideration is given to how to support the resilience of the sector given the extensive pressures of this summer.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you very much for that, Cabinet Minister. The affected commoners in my constituency have already incurred almost £50,000 in direct costs and loss of earnings, with a further £20,000 needed for replacement fodder, and estimates for restoration work reaching around £89,000. In total, costs now exceed well over £100,000, with some family farms questioning their long-term liability. I've already written to your colleague the Cabinet Minister for rural resilience, looking for more support. And he came back and said pretty well that there wouldn't be any additional money because it was implied that sheep could just simply graze somewhere else, which I don't think were his words, but somebody had written on his behalf. And I'm sure he will disagree with that. I took great concern at that, as did many of the farming unions. However, we need a longer term solution to these issues. And given the scale of these losses—and across Wales—and the reality that these extreme events are likely to happen more often in the future, are you, Cabinet Minister, having discussions with ministerial colleagues about establishing a dedicated emergency fund designed to support farming businesses with managing short-term crises and financial challenges—not just a one-off, but a long-term fund?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch yn fawr am hynny, Weinidog Cabinet. Mae'r cominwyr yr effeithiwyd arnynt yn fy etholaeth i eisoes wedi wynebu bron i £50,000 o gostau uniongyrchol ac enillion a gollwyd, ac mae angen £20,000 arall ar gyfer porthiant amgen, gydag amcangyfrifon ar gyfer gwaith adfer yn cyrraedd tua £89,000. Mae cyfanswm y costau bellach ymhell dros £100,000, gyda rhai ffermydd teuluol yn cwestiynu eu hyfywedd hirdymor. Rwyf eisoes wedi ysgrifennu at eich cyd-Aelod, y Gweinidog Cabinet dros wydnwch gwledig, i ofyn am fwy o gymorth. Ac fe ddaeth yn ôl a dweud fwy neu lai na fyddai unrhyw arian ychwanegol gan mai'r awgrym oedd y gallai defaid bori yn rhywle arall, ac nid wyf yn meddwl mai ei eiriau ef oedd y rheini, ond roedd rhywun wedi eu hysgrifennu ar ei ran. Ac rwy'n siŵr y bydd yn anghytuno â hynny. Roeddwn yn pryderu'n fawr am hynny, fel llawer o'r undebau ffermio. Fodd bynnag, mae angen ateb mwy hirdymor i'r materion hyn. Ac o ystyried maint y colledion hyn—ac ar draws Cymru—a'r realiti fod y digwyddiadau eithafol hyn yn debygol o ddigwydd yn amlach yn y dyfodol, a ydych chi, Weinidog Cabinet, yn cael trafodaethau gyda chyd-Weinidogion ynglŷn â sefydlu cronfa argyfwng bwrpasol wedi'i chynllunio ar gyfer cynorthwyo busnesau ffermio i reoli argyfyngau tymor byr a heriau ariannol—nid cronfa untro, ond cronfa hirdymor?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for the supplementary question, and I'm sure it must have been a terrible summer for those farmers and commoners in your area and elsewhere in Wales where they faced these fires with very real consequences on how they did their farming and livestock farming. 

I have had discussions, and they continue, with the rural resilience Minister about the financial implications of both the direct fires and also such a difficult summer in terms of harvest and growing that the drought led to here in Wales. So, we'll continue those discussions. I'll discuss that particular letter with him as well.

But also, to the point you make about the longer term implications of what we face as a country, as a world, in terms of the different challenges that have really struck home this year, I think, in a way, that we've seen bits of it in the past, over the past few years where we've had some intense periods of heat and wildfire consequences, but we've never seen it in such a sustained way over such a long period of time. And so, this asks questions of our sustainable farming scheme. Of course, we've made the long-term financial commitment, multi-year, of £1 billion on that scheme, but we do need to look at the content of that scheme, going forward, in order to meet some of the challenges that were discussed yesterday, actually, in this Senedd over how we manage our uplands and mountain areas in particular.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am y cwestiwn atodol, ac rwy'n siŵr iddi fod yn haf ofnadwy i'r ffermwyr a'r cominwyr hynny yn eich ardal chi ac mewn mannau eraill yng Nghymru lle gwnaethant wynebu'r tanau hyn gyda chanlyniadau real iawn i'r ffordd yr oeddent yn ffermio ac yn ffermio da byw. 

Rwyf wedi cael trafodaethau, ac maent yn parhau, gyda'r Gweinidog gwydnwch gwledig am oblygiadau ariannol y tanau uniongyrchol a hefyd haf mor anodd o ran cynaeafu a thyfu yr arweiniodd y sychder ato yma yng Nghymru. Felly, byddwn yn parhau â'r trafodaethau hynny. Byddaf yn trafod y llythyr penodol hwnnw gydag ef hefyd.

Ond hefyd, ar y pwynt a wnewch am oblygiadau mwy hirdymor yr hyn a wynebwn fel gwlad, fel byd, o ran y gwahanol heriau sydd wedi taro i'r byw eleni, rwy'n credu, mewn ffordd, ein bod wedi gweld darnau ohono yn y gorffennol, dros y blynyddoedd diwethaf lle cawsom gyfnodau dwys o ganlyniadau gwres a thanau gwyllt, ond nid ydym erioed wedi ei weld mewn ffordd mor barhaus dros gyfnod mor hir o amser. Ac felly, mae hyn yn gofyn cwestiynau i'n cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy. Wrth gwrs, rydym wedi gwneud yr ymrwymiad ariannol hirdymor, amlflwyddyn, o £1 biliwn ar gyfer y cynllun hwnnw, ond mae angen inni edrych ar gynnwys y cynllun hwnnw wrth symud ymlaen, er mwyn goresgyn rhai o'r heriau a drafodwyd ddoe, mewn gwirionedd, yn y Senedd hon ynghylch sut rydym yn rheoli ein hucheldiroedd a'n hardaloedd mynyddig yn arbennig.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, a fortnight ago, I attended the defence security and resilience conference in Newport, something rather naively described by opponents as an arms fair. It wasn't an arms fair. Resilience was a really key part of it, and some of these discussions we've had featured there highly in terms of flooding and wildfires. The First Minister yesterday quite rightly referred to resilience several times in his statement regarding the wildfires, and, indeed, we have a Cabinet member that has that word in the description. So, my question is, really: looking as to when these events occur in the future, and we do need to build into our land management more resilience—things like firebreaks and ponds, and so on—is the Minister prepared to talk about the financial impacts of the sustainable farming scheme, in particular, in terms of working into that scheme how we can build more resilience into our system so that we can prevent the extent of these fires in future?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, bythefnos yn ôl, mynychais y gynhadledd ar ddiogelwch amddiffyn a gwydnwch yng Nghasnewydd, rhywbeth a ddisgrifiwyd yn eithaf naïf gan wrthwynebwyr fel ffair arfau. Nid ffair arfau oedd hi. Roedd gwydnwch yn rhan allweddol iawn o'r digwyddiad, ac roedd rhai o'r trafodaethau rydym wedi'u cael yn cael lle amlwg yno o ran llifogydd a thanau gwyllt. Cyfeiriodd y Prif Weinidog ddoe at wydnwch sawl gwaith yn ei ddatganiad ynglŷn â'r tanau gwyllt, ac yn wir, mae gennym aelod o'r Cabinet sydd â'r gair hwnnw yn y disgrifiad. Felly, dyma fy nghwestiwn: pan fydd y digwyddiadau hyn yn digwydd yn y dyfodol, mae angen inni ymgorffori mwy o wydnwch yn ein dulliau o reoli tir—pethau fel strimynnau atal tân a phyllau dŵr, ac ati—a yw'r Gweinidog yn barod i siarad am effeithiau ariannol y cynllun ffermio cynaliadwy, yn enwedig, o ran ymgorffori yn y cynllun hwnnw sut y gallwn adeiladu mwy o wydnwch i mewn i'n system fel y gallwn atal cyrhaeddiad y tanau hyn yn y dyfodol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Yes, I agree, and I'm sure this summer has brought it home to the Minister, just as much as it has to farmers, how we manage land. Farmers knew this already, by the way. They were telling Ministers, I think, over the years about how some of the changes in support schemes are having effects on our uplands. But this year has brought to the forefront how there is a very direct relationship with how we farm our uplands and what happens in those uplands, both in terms of wildlife and regeneration of wildlife, but also in how we manage the uplands both in order to prevent floods downstream and also to ensure that we have adequate measures for limiting wildfires in these excessive heat situations that we have.

We are facing and we are likely to have to plan for these events to become possibly even annual events. We know that our climate is changing, and we as a Government and as a Senedd need to own up to that fact and to take the measures that we need to in order to make Wales resilient in the nature of the climate change that we are seeing in our society.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n cytuno, ac rwy'n siŵr bod yr haf hwn wedi dangos i'r Gweinidog, lawn cymaint ag y mae wedi ei wneud i ffermwyr, sut rydym yn rheoli tir. Roedd ffermwyr yn gwybod hyn eisoes, gyda llaw. Roeddent yn dweud wrth Weinidogion dros y blynyddoedd sut y mae rhai o'r newidiadau i gynlluniau cymorth yn cael effaith ar ein hucheldiroedd. Ond mae eleni wedi amlygu sut y mae perthynas uniongyrchol iawn â'r ffordd rydym yn ffermio ein hucheldiroedd a beth sy'n digwydd yn yr ucheldiroedd hynny, o ran bywyd gwyllt ac adfywio bywyd gwyllt, ond hefyd y ffordd y rheolwn yr ucheldiroedd er mwyn atal llifogydd i lawr yr afon a hefyd i sicrhau bod gennym fesurau digonol ar gyfer cyfyngu ar danau gwyllt yn y cyfnodau o wres gormodol a gawn.

Rydym yn wynebu, ac mae'n debygol y bydd yn rhaid inni gynllunio i'r digwyddiadau hyn ddod yn ddigwyddiadau blynyddol o bosibl. Rydym yn gwybod bod ein hinsawdd yn newid, ac mae angen i ni fel Llywodraeth ac fel Senedd gyfaddef hynny a rhoi'r mesurau sydd eu hangen arnom ar waith er mwyn gwneud Cymru'n wydn i natur y newid hinsawdd a welwn yn ein cymdeithas.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Weinidog, fel gwnes i sôn wrth y Prif Weinidog ddoe, fe wnaeth y tân dinistriol yn Pantside ddangos yn glir iawn sut mae'r perygl o danau wedi newid. Cafodd cartrefi yn fanno eu dinistrio ac, a dweud y gwir, roeddem ni'n lwcus iawn bod neb wedi colli eu bywydau. Mae'r diffoddwyr tân dwi wedi siarad efo nhw trwy'r Fire Brigades Union yn glir bod y digwyddiadau hyn yn cynyddu o ran maint, cymhlethdod a'r adnoddau sydd eu hangen i ymateb iddyn nhw. Felly, ochr yn ochr â chymorth i'r commoners ac i'r ffermwyr sydd wedi dioddef colledion, pa asesiad ydych chi wedi ei wneud o oblygiadau ariannol ehangach tanau yr haf yma?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Minister, as I mentioned to the First Minister yesterday, the devastating fire in Pantside clearly demonstrated how the risk of wildfires has changed. Homes there were destroyed and, frankly, we were very fortunate that no lives were lost. The firefighters that I've spoken to through the FBU are clear that these incidents are increasing in terms of scale, complexity and the resources required to respond to them. Therefore, alongside the support for commoners and farmers who have suffered losses, what assessment have you made of the wider financial implications of this summer's fires?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch am y cwestiwn a diolch am ein hatgoffa ni o'r golygfeydd ofnadwy yna welon ni yn Pantside yn eich ardal chi, gyda'r tanau yna yn y gymuned yna yn dangos bod eiddo a thai hefyd mewn peryg mewn sefyllfaoedd o’r math yma. Mae’r Gweinidog llywodraeth leol eisoes wedi cytuno i agor yr emergency financial assistance scheme. Felly, mae hwnna ar gael ar gyfer yr awdurdodau lleol a’r awdurdodau tân i asesu maint y gwariant ychwanegol yr oedden nhw wedi gorfod ei wynebu yn ystod yr haf yma, a sut y gallan nhw, os oes angen, ddefnyddio’r cynllun yna. Rŷn ni’n derbyn bod y gwaith maen nhw wedi'i wneud fel diffoddwyr tân, fel awdurdodau lleol, fel cymunedau lleol, yn arbennig o bwysig yn ein cymdeithas ni, ac rŷn ni'n ddiolchgar am y gwaith yna yn ystod yr haf. Felly, rŷn ni'n barod i edrych gyda'r awdurdodau perthnasol ar sut mae'n bosib ariannu unrhyw arian sydd ei angen arnyn nhw. Byddwn ni'n cydweithio gyda nhw ar hynny.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you for that question and thank you for reminding us of those terrible scenes that we saw in Pantside in your own constituency, with the fires affecting that community showing that property and homes are also at risk in scenarios such as this. The Minister for local government has already agreed to open the emergency financial assistance scheme and, therefore, that is available for local authorities and fire authorities in order to assess the scale of additional expenditure that they faced during this summer, and how they can, if necessary, use that programme. We accept that the work that they did as firefighters and local authorities and local communities is extremely important for our communities, and we are grateful for that work done over the summer. Therefore, we are willing to look, along with the appropriate authorities, as to the funding of any moneys that they require. We will be working with them on that.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 5. Pa waith y mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet yn ei wneud i ddiwygio ardrethi busnes ar gyfer busnesau lletygarwch? OQ64459
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 5. What work is the Cabinet Minister undertaking to reform business rates for hospitality businesses? OQ64459

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Ddoe, roeddwn i'n falch iawn i gyhoeddi cymorth ardrethi annomestig newydd i fusnesau lletygarwch a hamdden, sydd wrth galon ein huchelgais i adfywio canol trefi. O 1 Ebrill 2027 ymlaen, bydd busnesau cymwys yn elwa ar ostyngiad parhaol o 30 y cant yn eu biliau ardrethi.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yesterday, I was pleased to announce new non-domestic rates support for hospitality and leisure businesses, which are central to our ambition to regenerate town centres. From 1 April 2027 onwards, eligible businesses will benefit from a permanent 30 per cent reduction in their rates bills.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. I welcome the Cabinet Minister's announcement of a 30 per cent cut to business rates for hospitality and leisure businesses. This will be a vital lifeline to small hospitality and leisure businesses and has already been welcomed by businesses in Ceredigion Penfro. These small businesses play essential roles in our rural and coastal communities, protecting local jobs, strengthening local economies and building lasting prosperity. I'm happy to see that this announcement extends beyond just pubs, clubs and live music venues, like in England, to support visitor accommodation and leisure businesses like hotels, cinemas, theatres, museums and gyms. With this in mind, can the Minister explain what she anticipates now will be the practical impact of these measures for towns and high streets across Wales, as well as in our constituency of Ceredigion Penfro?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Rwy'n croesawu cyhoeddiad y Gweinidog Cabinet y bydd toriad o 30 y cant i ardrethi busnes yn cael ei gyflwyno ar gyfer busnesau lletygarwch a hamdden. Bydd hyn yn rhaff achub hanfodol i fusnesau lletygarwch a hamdden bach ac mae'r newyddion eisoes wedi'i groesawu gan fusnesau yng Ngheredigion Penfro. Mae'r busnesau bach hyn yn chwarae rolau hanfodol yn ein cymunedau gwledig ac arfordirol, gan ddiogelu swyddi lleol, cryfhau economïau lleol ac adeiladu ffyniant parhaol. Rwy'n falch o weld bod y cyhoeddiad hwn yn ymestyn y tu hwnt i dafarndai, clybiau a lleoliadau cerddoriaeth fyw yn unig, fel sy'n digwydd yn Lloegr, i gefnogi busnesau llety ymwelwyr a hamdden fel gwestai, sinemâu, theatrau, amgueddfeydd a champfeydd. Gyda hyn mewn golwg, a all y Gweinidog egluro beth y mae'n ei ragweld nawr fydd effaith ymarferol y mesurau hyn ar drefi a strydoedd mawr ledled Cymru, yn ogystal ag yn ein hetholaeth ni yng Ngheredigion Penfro?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Ces i gic gan y Dirprwy Lywydd, dwi'n meddwl, i gadw fy atebion i'n fyrrach. Felly, fe wnaf i ymdrechu i wneud hynny. Ni wnaf i ddim ail-ddweud dim gwnes i ei ddweud ddoe yn Senedd, pan oeddem ni'n trafod y gostyngiad treth yma o 30 y cant. Dwi'n gobeithio ei fod e'n cyflawni dau beth. Dwi'n gobeithio ei fod e'n gwneud gwahaniaeth realistig i'r busnesau yma a fydd yn elwa o hyn, ac y byddan nhw yn teimlo ei fod e'n eu galluogi nhw i gynllunio'n well ar gyfer y dyfodol oherwydd bod hyn yn barhaol. Ond hefyd gobeithio ei fod e'n cyflawni neges o gefnogaeth oddi wrth y Llywodraeth yma, a'r Senedd yma os bydd pawb yn cytuno i'r rheoliadau, ein bod ni o ddifri yn moyn gweld y sector yma yn cael ei chefnogi ac yn elwa ac yn datblygu yn y cymunedau yna ar draws Cymru sy'n mynd i elwa—nid dim ond y rhai arfordirol yn eich etholaeth chi a fi, ond hefyd y canol trefi yna, y swbwrbia yna hefyd, yn ein dinasoedd ni ac yn ein cymunedau ôl-lofaol ni.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you. I was nudged by the Deputy Presiding Officer to keep my answers shorter, so I'll make an effort to do that. I won't repeat what I said yesterday in the Senedd when we were discussing this rate reduction of 30 per cent. But I do hope that it achieves two things. I hope that it makes a real difference to these businesses that will benefit from this, and that they will feel that it will enable them to plan more effectively for the future because this is a permanent cut. But also I hope that it delivers a message of support from this Government, and this Senedd if everyone agrees to the regulations, that we are serious about seeing this sector being supported and benefiting and developing in those communities across Wales that will benefit—not just those in coastal areas in our constituency, but also those town centres and suburbia too in our cities, towns and post-industrial communities.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: O fewn Llywodraeth Cymru, y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio sy'n uniongyrchol gyfrifol am lywodraeth leol, ond rŷn ni'n ymwybodol ar draws y Llywodraeth o'r pwysau ariannol ar gynghorau sir wrth iddynt ddelifro gwasanaethau cyhoeddus pwysig.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Within the Welsh Government, responsibility for local government lies with my colleague the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning, but we are aware across the Government that there is financial pressure on local authorities as they deliver important public services.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Cabinet Minister, councils across Wales are at breaking point. Council tax rises this year have already added around £104 on average to band D bills across Powys, Neath Port Talbot and indeed Swansea, yet people are still paying more whilst roads crumble and front-line services disappear too. And now we are losing our primary schools. Cradoc primary school, for instance, in a nearby village to me, has already closed. When a primary school is closed, it's ripping out the heart of our communities. And clearly, under this Plaid Government, more school closures are coming too. My main question is this: as you have now commissioned a review of the funding formula, including rurality and sparsity, will you now admit that the current system is failing, and will you guarantee fairer funding, so taxpayers aren't continually asked to pay more for less, while our communities lose their services and more children lose their primary schools too? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Weinidog Cabinet, mae cynghorau ledled Cymru ar ben eu tennyn. Mae codiadau yn y dreth gyngor eleni eisoes wedi ychwanegu oddeutu £104 ar gyfartaledd at filiau band D ym Mhowys, Castell-nedd Port Talbot, ac yn wir, yn Abertawe, ond mae pobl yn dal i dalu mwy tra bo ffyrdd yn malu a gwasanaethau rheng flaen yn diflannu hefyd. A nawr, rydym yn colli ein hysgolion cynradd. Mae ysgol gynradd Cradoc, er enghraifft, mewn pentref cyfagos i mi, eisoes wedi cau. Pan fydd ysgol gynradd yn cau, mae'n rhwygo calon ein cymunedau. Ac yn amlwg, o dan y Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru hon, bydd rhagor o ysgolion yn cau hefyd. Fy mhrif gwestiwn yw hwn: a chithau bellach wedi comisiynu adolygiad o'r fformiwla gyllido, gan gynnwys gwledigrwydd a theneurwydd poblogaeth, a wnewch chi gyfaddef nawr fod y system bresennol yn methu, ac a wnewch chi warantu cyllid tecach, fel na fydd trethdalwyr yn gorfod talu mwy am lai o hyd ac o hyd, tra bo'n cymunedau'n colli eu gwasanaethau a mwy o blant yn colli eu hysgolion cynradd hefyd? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I represent a rural community, and have done over the years, so I'm very familiar with the fact that there are many factors that are at play in designing and deciding on the future of rural schools. It is not just the availability of public funding. Rural communities and aspects within those rural communities are a challenge, especially when we think about the depopulation, especially of our younger population, from many of our rural communities. How we look across Government as to how we can support that, not just in terms of money, but in how we are designing support, housing and economic opportunity for our rural areas, is important.

The important piece of work that this Government has started, though, is how we design a local government formula that meets the complexity of needs that our local authorities have. You rightly identified two of them in rurality and sparsity and the difficulty and expensive nature of delivering services across rural and sparse areas. We had reference made earlier to other priorities as well in terms of socioeconomic deprivation. Making sure that we strike a better balance in how we can deliver services effectively to all our communities in Wales is the journey that this Government has commenced in this piece of work, and hopefully all of us can involve ourselves in that.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n cynrychioli cymuned wledig, ac rwyf wedi gwneud hynny dros y blynyddoedd, felly rwy'n ymwybodol fod llawer o ffactorau i'w hystyried wrth lunio a phenderfynu ar ddyfodol ysgolion gwledig. Nid oes a wnelo hyn ag argaeledd cyllid cyhoeddus yn unig. Mae cymunedau gwledig ac agweddau o fewn y cymunedau gwledig hynny yn her, yn enwedig pan fyddwn yn meddwl am y diboblogi, yn enwedig ein poblogaeth iau, o lawer o'n cymunedau gwledig. Mae'r ffordd yr edrychwn ar draws y Llywodraeth ar sut y gallwn gefnogi hynny, nid yn unig o ran arian, ond o ran sut rydym yn llunio cymorth, tai a chyfleoedd economaidd ar gyfer ein hardaloedd gwledig, yn bwysig.

Y gwaith pwysig y mae'r Llywodraeth hon wedi'i ddechrau, fodd bynnag, yw sut rydym yn llunio fformiwla llywodraeth leol sy'n diwallu cymhlethdod anghenion ein hawdurdodau lleol. Fe wnaethoch chi nodi dau ohonynt, yn gywir ddigon, sef gwledigrwydd a theneurwydd poblogaeth ac anhawster a natur ddrud darparu gwasanaethau mewn ardaloedd gwledig a phrin eu poblogaeth. Cyfeiriwyd yn gynharach at flaenoriaethau eraill hefyd o ran amddifadedd economaidd-gymdeithasol. Sicrhau ein bod yn taro gwell cydbwysedd o ran y ffordd y gallwn ddarparu gwasanaethau'n effeithiol i'n holl gymunedau yng Nghymru yw'r daith y mae'r Llywodraeth hon wedi cychwyn arni gyda'r gwaith hwn, a gobeithio y gall pob un ohonom chwarae ein rhan yn hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae'r rhagolygon ar gyfer cyllideb Cymru yn dal i fod yn hynod heriol. Mae disgwyl i’r cyllid adnoddau ostwng 0.7 y cant mewn termau real yn 2027-28 a bydd cyllidebau cyfalaf yn gostwng dros y tair blynedd nesaf, o’i gyferbynnu â'r twf cyfartalog o 3.5 y cant y flwyddyn mewn termau real a welwyd ddechrau'r degawd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The outlook for the Welsh budget remains extremely challenging. The expectation is that resource funding will fall 0.7 per cent in real terms in 2027-28 and that capital budgets will decline over the next three years, in contrast to the average real-terms growth of 3.5 per cent per year seen since the start of the decade.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: It's always interesting when you decide where you want to start something, because if you started in 2011, you'd have seen an entirely different figure. But let's not argue over that. Whilst every organisation believes it needs more money, fairness is important. What we know is that in devolved areas, Wales gets 20 per cent more than England for the same service. A commission led by Gerry Holtham calculated that Wales needs 15 per cent more than England for the same service. Wales has a Barnett floor set at that 15 per cent level. What evidence does the Minister have that the Holtham commission was wrong?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae bob tro'n ddiddorol pan fyddwch chi'n penderfynu ble rydych chi am ddechrau rhywbeth, oherwydd pe byddech chi wedi dechrau yn 2011, byddech wedi gweld ffigur hollol wahanol. Ond gadewch inni beidio â dadlau ynglŷn â hynny. Er bod pob sefydliad yn credu bod angen mwy o arian arno, mae tegwch yn bwysig. Yr hyn a wyddom, mewn meysydd datganoledig, yw bod Cymru’n cael 20 y cant yn fwy na Lloegr am yr un gwasanaeth. Cyfrifodd comisiwn dan arweiniad Gerry Holtham fod angen 15 y cant yn fwy ar Gymru na Lloegr am yr un gwasanaeth. Mae gan Gymru lawr Barnett wedi'i osod ar y lefel honno o 15 y cant. Pa dystiolaeth sydd gan y Gweinidog fod comisiwn Holtham yn anghywir?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Finance
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I don't dispute the Holtham commission. I don't dispute the point you made at the start that wherever you start your analysis of any data, you can assess that. I'm trying to think of how we think about public service delivery now in the post-COVID period. That's why I was identifying this decade only. But you and I were in Senedds of the past where those austerity years of public finance in Wales, under a different political regime at a UK level, were particularly difficult at that time as well. So, I'm not pitching one difficult time against another. We have faced many of them in this place. I actually go back long enough to remember a time of plenty as well in this place, but that was another decade, almost in another century.

On the point you make, though, about needing to properly now assess where we are in terms of fiscal equality and meeting the economic and social needs of Wales through the Barnett formula as it is currently, our view as a Government is that the Barnett formula needs review. My immediate view on that—and it's something that I shared with the previous finance Minister—is that the Barnett formula especially needs its operational aspects to be strengthened. So, we need greater transparency on the Barnett formula as it exists, as well as independent oversight of the Barnett formula, so that we never ever again have to deal with the fiasco as it was of the decision on HS2 and how that has underfunded us as a country. And on that, if not on any other issue, I hope that we can all unite.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Nid wyf yn honni bod comisiwn Holtham yn anghywir. Nid wyf yn anghytuno â'r pwynt a wnaethoch ar y dechrau, sef lle bynnag y byddwch yn dechrau eich dadansoddiad o unrhyw ddata, gallwch asesu hynny. Rwy'n ceisio meddwl sut rydym yn meddwl am ddarparu gwasanaethau cyhoeddus nawr yn y cyfnod ar ôl COVID. Dyna pam fy mod yn nodi'r degawd hwn yn unig. Ond roeddech chi a minnau yn rhan o Seneddau yn y gorffennol lle roedd blynyddoedd cyni cyllid cyhoeddus yng Nghymru, o dan drefn wleidyddol wahanol ar lefel y DU, yn arbennig o anodd bryd hynny hefyd. Felly, nid wyf yn gosod un cyfnod anodd yn erbyn y llall. Rydym wedi wynebu llawer ohonynt yn y lle hwn. Rwy'n mynd yn ôl yn ddigon hir i gofio cyfnod o ddigonedd hefyd yn y lle hwn, ond roedd hynny mewn degawd arall, mewn canrif arall bron â bod.

Ar y pwynt a wnewch, fodd bynnag, ynglŷn â'r angen i asesu'n iawn nawr ble rydym arni o ran cydraddoldeb cyllidol a diwallu anghenion economaidd a chymdeithasol Cymru drwy fformiwla Barnett fel y mae ar hyn o bryd, ein barn ni fel Llywodraeth yw bod angen adolygu fformiwla Barnett. Fy marn uniongyrchol ar hynny—ac mae'n rhywbeth a rannais gyda'r Gweinidog cyllid blaenorol—yw bod angen cryfhau agweddau gweithredol fformiwla Barnett yn arbennig. Felly, mae angen mwy o dryloywder arnom ar fformiwla Barnett fel y mae'n bodoli, yn ogystal â goruchwyliaeth annibynnol ar fformiwla Barnett, fel na fydd yn rhaid i ni byth eto ddelio â'r fath ffiasgo ag a welwyd yn sgil y penderfyniad ar HS2 a sut y mae hynny wedi ein tanariannu fel gwlad. Ac ar hynny, os nad ar unrhyw fater arall, rwy'n gobeithio y gall pob un ohonom fod yn gytûn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. I'd like to declare an interest, as I'm looking forward to becoming a trustee of the Living Room in the near future.

On 11 September this year, the Living Room in Cardiff celebrated 15 years of transforming people's lives. It was established by Wynford Ellis Owen with the support of the Welsh Council on Alcohol and Other Drugs, which itself is now marking 55 years of service. Since the beginning, the centre has offered hope to people living with addiction and harmful behaviours, as well as supporting their families and their local community.

Through counselling, therapeutic groups, peer support and education, thousands of people have had the opportunity to rebuild their lives. Stafell Fyw demonstrates that recovery is possible when people are treated with dignity, compassion and respect. It also highlights the value of investing in our community services, preventing problems from escalating and reducing pressure on our health, social care and criminal justice services.

As we mark this milestone, I'd like to thank the staff, volunteers, trustees and everyone who has contributed to the work of the Living Room over the last 15 years. Above all, I'd like to pay tribute to the individuals in recovery who remind us every day that change is possible and that hope is stronger than addiction.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Hoffwn ddatgan buddiant, gan fy mod yn edrych ymlaen at ddod yn un o ymddiriedolwyr Stafell Fyw yn y dyfodol agos.

Ar 11 Medi eleni, dathlodd Stafell Fyw yng Nghaerdydd 15 mlynedd o drawsnewid bywydau pobl. Fe'i sefydlwyd gan Wynford Ellis Owen gyda chefnogaeth Cyngor Cymru ar Alcohol a Chyffuriau Eraill, sydd bellach yn nodi 55 mlynedd o wasanaeth. Ers y dechrau, mae'r ganolfan wedi cynnig gobaith i bobl sy'n byw gyda dibyniaeth ac ymddygiadau niweidiol, yn ogystal â chefnogi eu teuluoedd a'u cymuned leol.

Drwy gwnsela, grwpiau therapiwtig, cefnogaeth gan gymheiriaid ac addysg, mae miloedd o bobl wedi cael cyfle i ailadeiladu eu bywydau. Mae Stafell Fyw yn dangos bod adferiad yn bosibl pan gaiff pobl eu trin ag urddas, tosturi a pharch. Mae hefyd yn tynnu sylw at werth buddsoddi yn ein gwasanaethau cymunedol, gan atal problemau rhag gwaethygu a lleihau pwysau ar ein gwasanaethau iechyd, gofal cymdeithasol a chyfiawnder troseddol.

Wrth inni nodi'r garreg filltir hon, hoffwn ddiolch i'r staff, y gwirfoddolwyr, yr ymddiriedolwyr a phawb sydd wedi cyfrannu at waith Stafell Fyw dros y 15 mlynedd diwethaf. Yn anad dim, hoffwn dalu teyrnged i'r unigolion mewn adferiad sy'n ein hatgoffa bob dydd fod newid yn bosibl a bod gobaith yn gryfach na dibyniaeth.
