XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I too thank Paul Marr for the way he set this debate. That was really important. Because every victim of sexual exploitation, as we've heard, deserves justice. These are some of the most appalling crimes imaginable, and my heart—all of our hearts—goes out to everyone who has been a victim. And that is why this debate is so important.

The recent rise in convictions in Wales should serve as a reminder that this is not an issue that can simply be dismissed or something that happens elsewhere. Recent cases in Wales demonstrate that child sexual exploitation has occurred here in our communities, and that serious questions must continue to be asked about whether agencies always acted as they should have. 

We welcome the UK Government's decision to establish a statutory independent inquiry into grooming gangs. It is an important step forward, and one that survivors have campaigned for over many years. But whilst that inquiry is welcome, it cannot be used as an excuse for inaction here in Wales.

Our amendment calls on the Welsh Government to commission a Wales-wide grooming gang inquiry into matters that fall within devolved competence. That is a reasonable request. Indeed, it's difficult to see how anyone could oppose it. Schools, social services, safeguarding arrangements, health services and local authorities are all devolved, as we've heard from previous speakers. If failures occurred within any of those systems, surely it's the responsibility of the Welsh Government and the Senedd to understand what happened, to learn from it, and to ensure that no child is ever failed in the same way again.

A Wales-wide inquiry would not duplicate the work of a UK inquiry; it would complement it by focusing specifically on Welsh institutions, Welsh services, Welsh safeguarding systems, and Welsh decision making. It would allow victims in Wales to have confidence that their experiences are being listened to and properly examined. Many survivors have spent years fighting to be heard. They have shown remarkable courage in speaking publicly about their experiences, and in demanding that institutions examine what went wrong. We owe it to them to pursue every avenue that can help uncover the truth and deliver meaningful change. If there were failures within devolved Welsh services, then those failures must be identified. 

So, today, I urge Members from across the Chamber to support our amendment. We must send a clear message that, wherever these crimes occur, and whatever institutions may be involved, we will always put the pursuit of truth, justice and the protection of children first. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwyf innau hefyd yn diolch i Paul Marr am y ffordd y gosododd y ddadl hon. Roedd hynny'n bwysig iawn. Oherwydd mae pob dioddefwr camfanteisio rhywiol, fel y clywsom, yn haeddu cyfiawnder. Dyma rai o'r troseddau mwyaf ofnadwy y gellir eu dychmygu, ac mae fy nghalon—ein calonnau ni i gyd—yn gwaedu dros bawb sydd wedi bod yn ddioddefwr. A dyna pam y mae'r ddadl hon mor bwysig.

Dylai'r cynnydd diweddar mewn euogfarnau yng Nghymru ein hatgoffa nad yw hwn yn fater y gellir ei ddiystyru neu rywbeth sy'n digwydd mewn mannau eraill. Mae achosion diweddar yng Nghymru yn dangos bod camfanteisio'n rhywiol ar blant wedi digwydd yma yn ein cymunedau, a bod rhaid parhau i ofyn cwestiynau difrifol ynglŷn ag a yw asiantaethau bob amser wedi gweithredu fel y dylent.

Rydym yn croesawu penderfyniad Llywodraeth y DU i sefydlu ymchwiliad annibynnol statudol i gangiau grŵmio. Mae'n gam pwysig ymlaen, ac yn un y mae goroeswyr wedi ymgyrchu drosto ers nifer o flynyddoedd. Ond er bod yr ymchwiliad hwnnw i'w groesawu, ni ellir ei ddefnyddio fel esgus dros ddiffyg gweithredu yma yng Nghymru.

Mae ein gwelliant ni'n galw ar Lywodraeth Cymru i gomisiynu ymchwiliad gangiau grŵmio ledled Cymru i faterion o fewn y cymhwysedd datganoledig. Mae hwnnw'n gais rhesymol. Yn wir, mae'n anodd gweld sut y gallai unrhyw un ei wrthwynebu. Mae ysgolion, gwasanaethau cymdeithasol, trefniadau diogelu, gwasanaethau iechyd ac awdurdodau lleol i gyd wedi'u datganoli, fel y clywsom gan siaradwyr blaenorol. Os digwyddodd methiannau yn unrhyw un o'r systemau hynny, mae'n sicr mai cyfrifoldeb Llywodraeth Cymru a'r Senedd yw deall beth a ddigwyddodd, dysgu ohono, a sicrhau nad oes unrhyw blentyn yn cael cam yn yr un ffordd eto.

Ni fyddai ymchwiliad ledled Cymru yn dyblygu gwaith ymchwiliad y DU; byddai'n ei ategu trwy ganolbwyntio'n benodol ar sefydliadau Cymru, gwasanaethau Cymru, systemau diogelu Cymru, a phenderfyniadau a wneir yng Nghymru. Byddai'n caniatáu i ddioddefwyr yng Nghymru gael hyder fod eu profiadau'n cael eu clywed a'u harchwilio'n briodol. Mae llawer o oroeswyr wedi treulio blynyddoedd yn brwydro i gael eu clywed. Maent wedi dangos dewrder rhyfeddol wrth siarad yn gyhoeddus am eu profiadau, ac wrth fynnu bod sefydliadau'n archwilio beth aeth o'i le. Mae arnom ddyletswydd iddynt i ddilyn pob llwybr a all helpu i ddatgelu'r gwir a chyflawni newid ystyrlon. Os oes methiannau yng ngwasanaethau datganoledig Cymru, rhaid nodi'r methiannau hynny. 

Felly, heddiw, rwy'n annog Aelodau o bob rhan o'r Siambr i gefnogi ein gwelliant. Ble bynnag y bydd y troseddau hyn yn digwydd, a pha sefydliadau bynnag a allai fod ynghlwm wrthynt, rhaid inni anfon neges glir y byddwn bob amser yn rhoi mynd ar drywydd y gwirionedd, cyfiawnder a diogelu plant yn gyntaf. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
There are some words and some subjects that are uncomfortable to discuss. There are words that our politicians and institutions would rather avoid—words like 'grooming gang'—and therein lies the problem. When the safety of children is at stake, discomfort cannot be an excuse for silence. So, in this debate, I want to speak about the organised sexual exploitation of children, which has commonly become known as the 'grooming gang scandal'. 

These words should never be abstract. They are real, and there are real victims of it. Behind every report, every investigation, every statistic, is a child: a child who should have been protected; a child who should have been listened to; far too often, a child who was failed by the very institutions that were designed to keep them safe. 

The independent inquiry into child sex abuse examined organised sexual exploitation across England and Wales. Wales was not absent from its findings, and in the new statutory inquiry, it does not automatically guarantee that a particular Welsh town or local authority will receive a full investigation.

In Swansea, the inquiry was initially told that there was no data suggesting sexual exploitation by networks of gang-related child abuse. In response to our freedom of information request in 2025, Gwent Police acknowledged that they only had the software available since 2017 to search the 6,683 sexual offences recorded, and they were not sure if ethnicity was recorded, and if it was, it would cost too much manpower and time to trawl through the data to search for grooming cases. Yet the inquiry found examples of exploitation by groups that should have been identified by the police. South Wales Police itself acknowledges the likelihood that organised criminal networks existed that had not been discovered. This is shameful. How do we protect our children from something that the authorities fail to identify? We cannot properly understand the threat if we refuse to collect the data to expose it.

The independent inquiry, therefore, made an extremely important recommendation: police forces and local authorities should collect specific information on known and suspected child sexual exploitation networks, including data on sex, ethnicity and disability of victims and perpetrators. And that is not prejudice, it's evidence. If patterns exist, we need to know about them. If particular vulnerabilities are being exploited, we need to know of them. Wherever offenders come from, their ethnicity, religion, background and status, the response should be exactly the same. Protect the child, investigate the crime, prosecute the offender for a long time, and do not let them out early. No excuses, no political sensitivities, no fear of embarrassment, and no institution protecting its reputation ahead of a vulnerable child. We value children above protecting the very systems that let them down.

And we should also remember something fundamental about grooming: children who are manipulated, coerced and exploited are the victims. They are not responsible for the crimes committed against them. A frightened teenager who has been groomed by adults does not need an institution finding reasons not to intervene. They need an adult to listen. They need professionals to recognise the warning signs, and they need the state to act. This means schools, social services, health professionals, local authorities and police sharing information effectively.

Let's narrow this down to Wales. So, where are the Welsh authorities targeted for investigation in the statutory review? So far, there aren't any. Are we to be pushed back again, not listening in Wales again? Are the victims ever going to get the justice that they deserve in Wales? In short, we want data accuracy; we want transparency; Welsh voices to be heard; and they must not be silenced ever again.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae yna rai geiriau a rhai pynciau sy'n anghyfforddus i'w trafod. Mae yna eiriau y byddai'n well gan ein gwleidyddion a'n sefydliadau eu hosgoi—geiriau fel 'gangiau grŵmio'—a dyna'r broblem. Pan fydd diogelwch plant yn y fantol, ni all anghysur fod yn esgus dros dawelwch. Felly, yn y ddadl hon, rwyf am siarad am drosedd drefnedig camfanteisio'n rhywiol ar blant, a elwir yn gyffredin bellach fel y 'sgandal gangiau grŵmio'. 

Ni ddylai'r geiriau hyn byth fod yn haniaethol. Maent yn real, ac mae yna ddioddefwyr go iawn. Y tu ôl i bob adroddiad, pob ymchwiliad, pob ystadegyn, mae plentyn: plentyn a ddylai fod wedi cael ei ddiogelu; plentyn y dylid bod wedi gwrando arno; yn llawer rhy aml, plentyn a gafodd gam gan yr union sefydliadau a luniwyd i'w gadw'n ddiogel. 

Mae'r ymchwiliad annibynnol i gam-drin plant yn rhywiol yn archwilio camfanteisio rhywiol trefnedig ledled Cymru a Lloegr. Nid oedd Cymru'n absennol o'i ganfyddiadau, ac yn yr ymchwiliad statudol newydd, nid yw'n gwarantu'n awtomatig y bydd tref neu awdurdod lleol penodol yng Nghymru yn cael ymchwiliad llawn.

Yn Abertawe, dywedwyd wrth yr ymchwiliad yn wreiddiol nad oedd unrhyw ddata i awgrymu bod camfanteisio'n rhywiol gan rwydweithiau cam-drin plant yn gysylltiedig â gangiau'n digwydd. Mewn ymateb i'n cais rhyddid gwybodaeth yn 2025, cydnabu Heddlu Gwent mai dim ond ers 2017 y bu ganddynt y feddalwedd i chwilio'r 6,683 o droseddau rhywiol a gofnodwyd, ac nid oeddent yn sicr a oedd ethnigrwydd wedi'i gofnodi, ac os oedd, byddai'n costio gormod mewn adnoddau dynol ac amser i chwilio drwy'r data i chwilio am achosion o grŵmio. Ond canfu'r ymchwiliad enghreifftiau o gamfanteisio gan grwpiau a ddylai fod wedi cael eu nodi gan yr heddlu. Mae Heddlu De Cymru ei hun yn cydnabod y tebygolrwydd fod rhwydweithiau troseddol trefnedig yn bodoli nad oeddent wedi'u darganfod. Mae hyn yn gywilyddus. Sut y gallwn ddiogelu ein plant rhag rhywbeth y mae'r awdurdodau yn methu ei nodi? Ni allwn ddeall y bygythiad yn iawn os ydym yn gwrthod casglu'r data i'w ddatgelu.

Felly, fe wnaeth yr ymchwiliad annibynnol argymhelliad hynod bwysig: dylai heddluoedd ac awdurdodau lleol gasglu gwybodaeth benodol am rwydweithiau y gwyddys eu bod, ac yr amheuir eu bod yn camfanteisio'n rhywiol ar blant, gan gynnwys data ar ryw, ethnigrwydd ac anabledd y dioddefwyr a'r troseddwyr. Ac nid rhagfarn yw hynny, ond tystiolaeth. Os oes patrymau'n bodoli, mae angen inni wybod amdanynt. Os oes camfanteisio'n digwydd ar wendidau penodol, mae angen inni wybod amdanynt. O ble bynnag y daw'r troseddwyr, a beth bynnag yw eu hethnigrwydd, eu crefydd, eu cefndir a'u statws, dylai'r ymateb fod yn union yr un fath. Diogelu'r plentyn, ymchwilio i'r drosedd, dedfrydu'r troseddwr am gyfnod hir, a pheidio â'u rhyddhau'n gynnar. Dim esgusodion, dim sensitifrwydd gwleidyddol, dim ofn cywilydd, a dim sefydliad yn diogelu ei enw da yn hytrach na phlentyn bregus. Rydym ni'n rhoi gwerth uwch ar blant nag ar ddiogelu'r systemau a wnaeth gam â nhw.

A dylem gofio rhywbeth sylfaenol am grŵmio: plant sy'n cael eu manipiwleiddio, eu rheoli a'u hecsbloetio yw'r dioddefwyr. Nid nhw sy'n gyfrifol am y troseddau a gyflawnir yn eu herbyn. Nid yw unigolyn ifanc yn eu harddegau sydd wedi cael eu grŵmio gan oedolion angen sefydliad a ddaw o hyd i resymau dros beidio ag ymyrryd. Maent angen i oedolyn wrando arnynt. Maent angen i weithwyr proffesiynol adnabod yr arwyddion, ac maent angen i'r wladwriaeth weithredu. Mae hynny'n golygu bod angen i ysgolion, gwasanaethau cymdeithasol, gweithwyr iechyd proffesiynol, awdurdodau lleol a'r heddlu rannu gwybodaeth yn effeithiol.

Gadewch inni gyfyngu hyn i Gymru. Felly, ble mae'r awdurdodau Cymreig a dargedwyd ar gyfer eu hymchwilio yn yr adolygiad statudol? Hyd yma, nid oes unrhyw rai wedi'u targedu. A ydym yn mynd i gael ein gwthio'n ôl eto, a neb yn gwrando yng Nghymru eto? A yw'r dioddefwyr byth yn mynd i gael y cyfiawnder y maent yn ei haeddu yng Nghymru? Yn fyr, rydym eisiau data cywir; rydym eisiau tryloywder; i leisiau Cymreig gael eu clywed; ac ni ddylid eu tawelu byth eto.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I wanted to address those who truly matter at the centre of this: the women and children who have survived group-based sexual exploitation. I want to speak to everyone who has been in a vulnerable position and let down by those in power who were meant to be there to protect them.

My mum was barely 15 when she went to her GP and told him she was pregnant. His only advice was, 'Go home and tell your parents.' She was alone, she was frightened, and she hid it. Her teachers watched and shook their heads as the gossip spread around school while she used a ribbon to extend her school skirt around her growing baby. And three weeks after turning 16, my mum gave birth, and that was the first time that she'd been properly cared for by those who should have protected her. Too often, girls like my mum are judged on their bad choices rather than seen as children who needed help. I want every survivor to know that I hear you, I see you, and I believe you. You deserve support, and you deserve justice.

Quite often, what we've heard in debates is Reform inciting fear in minority groups. What we want to do is focus on what we would do to improve lives in Wales. It's so important that that is our focus. We all wish to make sure that we treat women as equal in our society and equal in this Chamber. We wish to hear and listen to every voice.

Reform position themselves as 'outside of the establishment', which obscures its own role in maintaining the political culture where male violence flourishes. This culture starts with harmless banter and women being spoken over, but it can escalate into intimidation, harassment, abuse and sexual violence. Here in Wales, specialist violence against women, domestic abuse and sexual violence services have warned of rising demand and increasingly complex high-risk cases, reminding us that violence against women is not an abstract issue, but a daily reality for far too many.

The system is still, too often, failing to deliver justice and protection, and changing that should be our collective commitment. Safety is not a slogan, it's a priority. Group-based abusers do not respect borders. We've heard how survivors have been trafficked across the UK and into Wales and out of Wales, so it's vital that we hear from everybody who has been in our country. This ensures that perpetrators are held to account.

Plaid Cymru's amendment is the right course of action because it puts victims and survivors first. Rather than duplicating efforts with a separate inquiry, we can work within the existing statutory framework to focus on what actually makes a difference—delivering the actions of the national strategy for prevention and responding to child sexual abuse. This is how we ensure that women and girls get the justice and support that they deserve.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Roeddwn i eisiau annerch y rhai sy'n wirioneddol bwysig yng nghanol hyn: y menywod a'r plant sydd wedi goroesi camfanteisio rhywiol gan grwpiau. Rwyf am siarad â phawb sydd wedi bod mewn sefyllfa fregus ac wedi'u siomi gan y rhai mewn grym a oedd i fod yno i'w hamddiffyn.

Roedd fy mam yn 15 oed pan aeth at ei meddyg teulu a dweud wrtho ei bod hi'n feichiog. Ei unig gyngor oedd, 'Ewch adref a dywedwch wrth eich rhieni.' Roedd hi ar ei phen ei hun, roedd hi'n ofnus, ac fe wnaeth hi ei guddio. Roedd ei hathrawon yn gwylio ac yn ysgwyd eu pennau wrth i'r clecs ledaenu o gwmpas yr ysgol wrth iddi ddefnyddio rhuban i ymestyn ei sgert ysgol o amgylch ei babi a oedd yn tyfu. A thair wythnos ar ôl ei phen-blwydd yn 16, rhoddodd fy mam enedigaeth, a dyna'r tro cyntaf iddi gael gofal priodol gan y rhai a ddylai fod wedi ei diogelu. Yn rhy aml, mae merched fel fy mam yn cael eu barnu ar eu dewisiadau gwael yn hytrach na'u gweld fel plant sydd angen help. Rwyf am i bob goroeswr wybod fy mod i'n eich clywed chi, rwy'n eich gweld chi, ac rwy'n eich credu chi. Rydych chi'n haeddu cefnogaeth, ac rydych chi'n haeddu cyfiawnder.

Yn aml, yr hyn a glywsom mewn dadleuon yw Reform yn cymell ofn mewn grwpiau lleiafrifol. Yr hyn rydym ni eisiau ei wneud yw canolbwyntio ar yr hyn y byddem yn ei wneud i wella bywydau yng Nghymru. Mae mor bwysig mai dyna yw ein ffocws. Rydym i gyd eisiau gwneud yn siŵr ein bod yn trin menywod yn gyfartal yn ein cymdeithas ac yn gyfartal yn y Siambr hon. Rydym am glywed a gwrando ar bob llais.

Mae Reform yn gosod eu hunain fel rhai 'ar y tu allan i'r sefydliad', sy'n cuddio ei rôl eu hunain yn cynnal y diwylliant gwleidyddol lle mae trais gan ddynion yn ffynnu. Mae'r diwylliant hwn yn dechrau gyda phryfocio diniwed a siarad dros ben menywod, ond gall ddwysáu'n fygythiad, aflonyddu, cam-drin a thrais rhywiol. Yma yng Nghymru, mae gwasanaethau arbenigol trais yn erbyn menywod, cam-drin domestig a thrais rhywiol wedi rhybuddio ynghylch galw cynyddol ac achosion risg uchel cynyddol gymhleth, gan ein hatgoffa nad mater haniaethol yw trais yn erbyn menywod, ond realiti dyddiol i lawer gormod o bobl.

Yn rhy aml, mae'r system yn dal i fethu sicrhau cyfiawnder ac amddiffyniad, a dylai newid hynny fod yn ymrwymiad ar y cyd. Nid slogan yw diogelwch, mae'n flaenoriaeth. Nid yw camdrinwyr sy'n gweithredu mewn grwpiau'n parchu ffiniau. Clywsom sut y mae goroeswyr wedi cael eu masnachu ledled y DU ac i mewn i Gymru ac allan o Gymru, felly mae'n hanfodol ein bod yn clywed gan bawb sydd wedi bod yn ein gwlad. Mae hyn yn sicrhau bod troseddwyr yn cael eu dwyn i gyfrif.

Gwelliant Plaid Cymru yw'r ffordd gywir o weithredu am ei fod yn rhoi dioddefwyr a goroeswyr yn gyntaf. Yn hytrach na dyblygu ymdrechion gydag ymchwiliad ar wahân, gallwn weithio o fewn y fframwaith statudol presennol i ganolbwyntio ar yr hyn sy'n gwneud gwahaniaeth mewn gwirionedd—cyflawni gweithredoedd y strategaeth genedlaethol ar gyfer atal ac ymateb i gam-drin plant yn rhywiol. Dyma sut y mae sicrhau bod menywod a merched yn cael y cyfiawnder a'r gefnogaeth y maent yn eu haeddu.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
The victims of these appalling crimes and their families deserve the truth. I'll begin by paying tribute to my colleague Paul Marr for the powerful and courageous way in which he opened this debate. Every Member here present, and those that could not be, should imagine being the victim or the parent fighting for answers, only to be ignored or failed by the authorities that are meant to protect them.

Grooming gangs represent some of the most sickening organised criminality our country has witnessed. Unless we establish the full scale of what has happened and confront the failures that allowed it to happen, we cannot protect children going forward. Last year, the Welsh Government claimed there were no current widespread issues with grooming gangs in Wales. Let's have a look at the past 10 weeks alone.

On 10 July, Azad Ahmed and Wasee Shikel were imprisoned in Cardiff. On 15 July, eight men were charged across south Wales as part of Operation Oak. On 3 August, five people in Rhyl were convicted of grooming gang offences. That is why our motion calls on the UK Government to ensure that Wales is investigated at the earliest opportunity as part of the statutory independent inquiry into grooming gangs. Victims in Wales deserve the same truth, the same justice and the same accountability as victims elsewhere in the United Kingdom. Those cases demand answers. How can the Welsh Government confidently claim there is no widespread problem when serious gaps remain in the evidence?

Reports elsewhere in Britain have identified cases involving predominantly Pakistani-heritage Muslim men targeting white British girls. For years, legitimate questions about those patterns were avoided by the authorities, who seemed more concerned about causing offence than protecting children. We cannot allow political correctness or institutional cowardice to stand in the way of safeguarding.

If similar patterns exist in Wales, they must be exposed. Transparent data on offender ethnicity is essential to understanding the threat and preventing further abuse. The Welsh Government must also scrutinise every relevant policy, including its nation of sanctuary approach, to ensure proper safeguards prevent dangerous individuals from entering or remaining in our communities.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae dioddefwyr y troseddau erchyll hyn a'u teuluoedd yn haeddu'r gwir. Rwyf am ddechrau drwy dalu teyrnged i'm cyd-Aelod Paul Marr am y ffordd bwerus a dewr yr agorodd y ddadl hon. Dylai pob Aelod yma, a'r rhai na allant fod yma, ddychmygu bod yn ddioddefwr neu'n rhiant yn ymladd am atebion, ddim ond i gael eu hanwybyddu neu eu siomi gan yr awdurdodau sydd i fod i'w diogelu.

Mae gangiau grŵmio'n cyflawni rhai o'r troseddau trefnedig mwyaf ffiaidd y mae ein gwlad wedi'u gweld. Oni bai ein bod yn cadarnhau graddau'r hyn sydd wedi digwydd ac yn wynebu'r methiannau a ganiataodd iddo ddigwydd, ni allwn ddiogelu plant yn y dyfodol. Y llynedd, honnodd Llywodraeth Cymru nad oedd unrhyw broblemau eang ar hyn o bryd gyda gangiau grŵmio yng Nghymru. Gadewch inni edrych ar y 10 wythnos diwethaf yn unig.

Ar 10 Gorffennaf, cafodd Azad Ahmed a Wasee Shikel eu carcharu yng Nghaerdydd. Ar 15 Gorffennaf, cyhuddwyd wyth dyn ar draws de Cymru yn rhan o Operation Oak. Ar 3 Awst, cafwyd pump o bobl yn y Rhyl yn euog o droseddau gangiau grŵmio. Dyna pam y mae ein cynnig yn galw ar Lywodraeth y DU i sicrhau bod Cymru’n cael ei hymchwilio cyn gynted â phosibl yn rhan o'r ymchwiliad annibynnol statudol i gangiau grŵmio. Mae dioddefwyr yng Nghymru yn haeddu'r un gwirionedd, yr un cyfiawnder a'r un atebolrwydd â dioddefwyr mewn mannau eraill yn y Deyrnas Unedig. Mae'r achosion hynny'n mynnu atebion. Sut y gall y Llywodraeth hon yng Nghymru honni'n hyderus nad oes problem eang pan fo bylchau difrifol yn y dystiolaeth o hyd?

Mae adroddiadau mewn mannau eraill ym Mhrydain wedi nodi achosion yn ymwneud â dynion Mwslimaidd o dras Pacistanaidd yn bennaf yn targedu merched gwyn Prydeinig. Am flynyddoedd, cafodd cwestiynau dilys am y patrymau hynny eu hosgoi gan yr awdurdodau, a oedd fel pe baent yn pryderu mwy am achosi tramgwydd na diogelu plant. Ni allwn ganiatáu i gywirdeb gwleidyddol na llwfrdra sefydliadol rwystro diogelu.

Os oes patrymau tebyg yng Nghymru, rhaid eu datgelu. Mae data tryloyw ar ethnigrwydd troseddwyr yn hanfodol i ddeall y bygythiad ac atal cam-drin pellach. Rhaid i Lywodraeth Cymru graffu hefyd ar bob polisi perthnasol, gan gynnwys ei chynllun cenedl noddfa, er mwyn sicrhau bod mesurau diogelwch priodol yn atal unigolion peryglus rhag dod i mewn i'n cymunedau neu aros ynddynt.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Does the Reform UK Member agree that anyone found guilty of abuse towards women and girls, regardless of their skin colour, should face the full weight of the law?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: A yw'r Aelod o Reform UK yn cytuno y dylai unrhyw un a geir yn euog o gam-drin menywod a merched, ni waeth beth y bo lliw eu croen, wynebu grym eithaf y gyfraith?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
An abuser is an abuser. Correct. Yes. 

Compassion cannot mean naivety. Anyone who comes to this country must respect our laws, our culture, and the rights of women and girls. We need to know whether social services, police forces and local authorities failed in their duty of care, whether warning signs were ignored, and most importantly, what has changed. Victims have waited far too long. They deserve truth, justice and accountability, and this Senedd must not rest until they receive them.

That's the speech over, but I've got a few minutes, so I've got free reign, Llywydd, if you don't mind. Some of the voices here today have been brilliant, and they've got to the heart of the problem. We have an issue going on across our land, and we need to grasp that mantle and do whatever we need to do to ensure our future generations and our young children now are safe and kept safe. There have been some brilliant points made from across the parties. Beca, I agree with many of the points that you made. This should not be a political football; it's a shame you never got the memo.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Camdriniwr yw camdriniwr. Cywir. Dylent.

Ni all tosturi olygu naïfrwydd. Rhaid i unrhyw un sy'n dod i'r wlad hon barchu ein cyfreithiau, ein diwylliant, a hawliau menywod a merched. Mae angen inni wybod a fethodd gwasanaethau cymdeithasol, heddluoedd ac awdurdodau lleol yn eu dyletswydd gofal, a anwybyddwyd y rhybuddion, ac yn bwysicaf oll, beth sydd wedi newid. Mae dioddefwyr wedi aros yn rhy hir o lawer. Maent yn haeddu'r gwirionedd, cyfiawnder ac atebolrwydd, ac mae’n rhaid i'r Senedd hon beidio â gorffwys hyd nes y'u cânt.

Dyna'r araith drosodd, ond mae gennyf ychydig funudau, felly mae gennyf rywfaint o ryddid, Lywydd, os nad oes ots gennych. Mae rhai o'r lleisiau yma heddiw wedi bod yn wych, ac maent wedi mynd at wraidd y broblem. Mae gennym broblem ledled y wlad, ac mae angen inni fynd i'r afael â hynny a gwneud beth bynnag sydd angen i ni ei wneud i sicrhau bod cenedlaethau'r dyfodol a'n plant ifanc nawr yn ddiogel ac yn cael eu cadw'n ddiogel. Mae rhai pwyntiau gwych wedi'u gwneud gan bob un o'r pleidiau. Beca, rwy'n cytuno â llawer o'r pwyntiau a wnaethoch. Ni ddylai hyn fod yn bêl-droed wleidyddol; mae'n drueni na chawsoch chi'r memo hwnnw.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you to all Members who've shared either their own experiences or family experiences. I would thank Paul for sharing the terrible—. Paul has gone out, but I will still put on the record the horrendous experience of his daughter, and the thoughts of everyone in the Chamber will of course be with her. I'm very grateful to him for sharing that.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i bob Aelod sydd wedi rhannu naill ai eu profiadau eu hunain neu brofiadau teuluol. Hoffwn ddiolch i Paul am rannu'r—. Mae Paul wedi mynd, ond hoffwn nodi profiad erchyll ei ferch, a bydd pawb yn y Siambr yn cydymdeimlo gyda hi, wrth gwrs. Rwy'n ddiolchgar iawn iddo am rannu hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae'r ddadl hon yn ymdrin â rhai o'r niweidiau mwyaf difrifol, mwyaf erchyll mae plentyn yn gallu eu profi. Mae cam-drin plant yn rhywiol a chamfanteisio rhywiol ar blant yn gallu cael effaith ddofn a gydol oes ar bob agwedd ar fywyd person. Maen nhw'n gallu effeithio ar addysg, perthnasoedd, cyflogaeth, iechyd corfforol, iechyd meddwl a llesiant unigolyn ymhell i'w fywyd fel oedolyn. Rhaid i'r rhai sy'n cyflawni y troseddau hyn gael eu dal i gyfrif. Mae pob dioddefwr a goroeswr yn haeddu cyfiawnder a chymorth.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: This debate deals with some of the most serious harms, the most horrific harms a child can experience. Child sexual abuse and child sexual exploitation can have a profound and lifelong impact on every aspect of a person's life. These issues can affect education, relationships, employment, physical health, mental health and well-being of an individual well into adulthood. Those who commit these crimes must be held to account. All victims and survivors deserve justice and help.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Before I go further, Llywydd, I want to acknowledge the courage of victims and survivors whose experiences continue to shape our understanding of abuse and exploitation and drive improvements across our safeguarding systems. I am in awe of your bravery, and I am committed to ensuring that your voices are heard and that your experiences continue to drive change.

The motion before us notes the recent rise in convictions relating to sexual exploitation by grooming gangs in Wales and states that all Welsh victims deserve justice. On that principle, there should be no disagreement in this Chamber. I would counter that it is not enough. Justice usually means a moment in time where people who have done awful things are held to account. That is vitally important. But in and of itself, it is not a deliverance. Survivors need the right support at the right time throughout their life and more than just that moment. That is why our amendment has added that crucial component of support.

The Government amendment further recognises that Wales falls within the scope of the statutory independent inquiry into grooming gangs, which has been established on an England and Wales basis. This Government is committed to considering carefully any findings and recommendations relating to Wales, and to progressing any necessary action with the utmost urgency. The amendment also reaffirms this Government's commitment to addressing child sexual abuse through the national strategy for preventing and responding to child sexual abuse in Wales 2026-2036, published in March this year, including implementing actions set out in its delivery plan.

Vital work has been undertaken in this area, building on the foundations that were laid previously, and the Government is engaging proactively with the inquiry. I hear the concerns raised around the Chamber—I hear them. We are undertaking and continuing official engagement, but I also have a forthcoming meeting with Baroness Longfield, and I will be raising these points. The inquiry has begun announcing areas for local investigation, as we've heard, and we do expect further areas to be announced as its work progresses. Wales already falls within the scope of the statutory inquiry, which can undertake detailed local investigations where the evidence warrants it. Indeed, as I say, I will be reinforcing the need for Wales to be considered fully when I meet the Baroness.

In terms of the motion, there are things we needed to add, like that point I was making about the support as well as justice, and recognising what this Government is doing.

Participation in a wider England and Wales inquiry also provides an opportunity to identify the trends and patterns of abuse that do not respect national borders.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Cyn imi fynd ymhellach, Lywydd, hoffwn gydnabod dewrder dioddefwyr a goroeswyr y mae eu profiadau'n parhau i lunio ein dealltwriaeth o gam-drin a chamfanteisio ac yn sbarduno gwelliannau ar draws ein systemau diogelu. Rwy'n llawn parch at eich dewrder, ac rwy'n ymrwymedig i sicrhau bod eich lleisiau'n cael eu clywed a bod eich profiadau'n parhau i sbarduno newid.

Mae'r cynnig ger ein bron yn nodi'r cynnydd diweddar mewn euogfarnau'n gysylltiedig â chamfanteisio rhywiol gan gangiau grŵmio yng Nghymru ac yn datgan bod pob dioddefwr yng Nghymru yn haeddu cyfiawnder. Ar yr egwyddor honno, ni ddylai fod unrhyw anghytundeb yn y Siambr hon. Buaswn yn ychwanegu nad yw hynny'n ddigon. Mae cyfiawnder fel arfer yn golygu adeg lle mae pobl sydd wedi gwneud pethau ofnadwy yn cael eu dwyn i gyfrif. Mae hynny'n hanfodol bwysig. Ond ynddo'i hun, nid yw hynny'n waredigaeth. Mae angen y gefnogaeth gywir ar oroeswyr ar yr adeg iawn drwy gydol eu hoes, a mwy na'r foment honno yn unig. Dyna pam y mae ein gwelliant wedi ychwanegu'r elfen hanfodol honno o gefnogaeth.

Mae gwelliant y Llywodraeth yn cydnabod ymhellach fod Cymru’n rhan o gwmpas yr ymchwiliad annibynnol statudol i gangiau grŵmio, sydd wedi'i sefydlu ar gyfer Cymru a Lloegr. Mae'r Llywodraeth hon wedi ymrwymo i ystyried yn ofalus unrhyw ganfyddiadau ac argymhellion yn ymwneud â Chymru, ac i fwrw ymlaen ag unrhyw gamau angenrheidiol gyda'r brys mwyaf. Mae'r gwelliant hefyd yn cadarnhau ymrwymiad y Llywodraeth hon i fynd i'r afael â cham-drin plant yn rhywiol drwy'r strategaeth genedlaethol ar atal ac ymateb i gam-drin plant yn rhywiol yng Nghymru 2026-2036, a gyhoeddwyd ym mis Mawrth eleni, gan gynnwys gweithredu'r camau a nodir yn ei chynllun cyflawni.

Mae gwaith hanfodol wedi'i wneud yn y maes hwn, gan adeiladu ar y sylfeini a osodwyd eisoes, ac mae'r Llywodraeth yn ymgysylltu'n rhagweithiol â'r ymchwiliad. Rwy'n clywed y pryderon a godwyd o amgylch y Siambr—rwy'n eu clywed. Rydym yn cynnal ac yn parhau i ymgysylltu'n swyddogol, ond mae gennyf gyfarfod ar y ffordd hefyd gyda'r Farwnes Longfield, a byddaf yn codi'r pwyntiau hyn. Mae'r ymchwiliad wedi dechrau cyhoeddi meysydd ar gyfer ymchwilio lleol, fel rydym wedi'i glywed, ac rydym yn disgwyl i feysydd pellach gael eu cyhoeddi wrth i'w waith fynd rhagddo. Mae Cymru eisoes yn rhan o gwmpas yr ymchwiliad statudol, a all gynnal ymchwiliadau lleol manwl lle mae'r dystiolaeth yn cyfiawnhau hynny. Yn wir, fel y dywedaf, byddaf yn atgyfnerthu'r angen i Gymru gael ei hystyried yn llawn pan fyddaf yn cyfarfod â'r Farwnes.

O ran y cynnig, mae yna bethau roedd angen i ni eu hychwanegu, fel y pwynt a wneuthum am y gefnogaeth yn ogystal â chyfiawnder, a chydnabod yr hyn y mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn ei wneud.

Mae cymryd rhan mewn ymchwiliad ehangach i Gymru a Lloegr hefyd yn gyfle i nodi'r tueddiadau a phatrymau camdriniaeth nad ydynt yn parchu ffiniau cenedlaethol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Bydd dysgu gwersi o’r ymchwiliad hwn yn hanfodol, ond mae hefyd yn bwysig iawn ein bod yn ymateb i realiti heddiw. Dyw’r plant sy’n wynebu risg heddiw ddim yn gallu aros am gasgliadau’r ymchwiliad. Ochr yn ochr â’n gwaith ar gyfer yr ymchwiliad, dŷn ni’n gwneud llawer o waith i gryfhau trefniadau diogelu ar draws Cymru, a bydd Aelodau yn clywed rhagor am hynny yn ystod yr wythnosau nesaf. Rwy'n edrych ymlaen at gyflwyno hynny.

Mae’r Ceidwadwyr Cymreig wedi cyflwyno gwelliant yn galw am ymchwiliad Cymru gyfan ac ar wahân i faterion wedi’u datganoli. Dwi’n deall y bwriad tu ôl i’r cynnig—dwi yn deall hynny. Mae’n bwysig ei gwneud yn glir, fel dwi wedi dweud, bod yr ymchwiliad ar gyfer Lloegr a Chymru. Mae Cymru’n rhan ganolog o’i gylch gwaith. Mae gan yr ymchwiliad y gallu i gynnal ymchwiliadau lleol yng Nghymru, ac mae’n cydnabod y cyfrifoldebau sydd wedi’u datganoli ac sydd ddim wedi'u datganoli. Roeddech chi'n sôn am ymgynghoriad COVID, a dwi'n meddwl mai dyna ydy'r gwahaniaeth mawr, oherwydd roedd hynna'n ymwneud â'r gwasanaeth iechyd yn bennaf, ac mae hwnna dan orchwyl Llywodraeth Cymru. Dyna'r gwahaniaeth—[Torri ar draws.] Mae Darren eisiau dod i mewn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Learning lessons from this inquiry will be essential, but it's also very important that we respond to today's reality. The children who are at risk today can't wait for the conclusions of the inquiry. Alongside our work for the inquiry, we are doing a lot of work to strengthen safeguarding arrangements across Wales, and Members will hear more about that in the coming weeks. I look forward very much to bringing that forward.  

The Welsh Conservatives have tabled an amendment calling for an all-Wales and separate inquiry for devolved issues. I understand the intention that is behind that proposal—I do understand that. It's important to clarify, as I've said, that the inquiry is for England and Wales, but Wales is a central part of its remit. The inquiry has the ability to conduct local investigations in Wales, and it recognises the responsibilities that are devolved and that are not devolved. You were talking about the COVID inquiry, and I think that's the big difference, because that related to the health service predominantly, and that comes under the Welsh Government's remit. That is the difference—[Interruption.] Darren wants to come in.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'm very grateful to you for taking the intervention. There's a direct parallel here, isn't there? Your party stood alongside my party calling for a Wales-specific COVID inquiry, because even though the UK COVID inquiry was charged with investigating matters in Wales, we did not believe that it was going to pay sufficient regard to the decision-making processes in Wales and those devolved areas of competence. Exactly the same applies here.

You've already said that you've had communications with Baroness Longfield about the local inquiries. She has replied the same to me as she has to correspondence from others in this Chamber to say that there may be further future local inquiries where the evidence leads. We already know there have been problems in Wales, so the evidence is already there, and yet we've seen at the moment no local inquiries initiated.

Surely you must see the challenge in the argument that you present now versus the argument you presented when the COVID inquiry decisions were being made, because we know that there are safeguarding issues in health, in social care, in housing, in all sorts of areas of devolved competence that we need to make sure are properly examined. That's why I would urge you—really seriously urge you—just to consider the position on this, and not give an outright 'No'. Even if you say, 'We'll keep an open mind on this', I'd be grateful.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n ddiolchgar iawn i chi am dderbyn yr ymyriad. Mae cyfatebiaeth uniongyrchol yma, onid oes? Safodd eich plaid ochr yn ochr â'm plaid i wrth alw am ymchwiliad COVID penodol i Gymru, oherwydd er bod ymchwiliad COVID y DU yn gyfrifol am ymchwilio i faterion yng Nghymru, nid oeddem yn credu y byddai'n rhoi digon o sylw i'r prosesau gwneud penderfyniadau yng Nghymru a'r meysydd cymhwysedd datganoledig hynny. Mae'r un peth yn union yn wir yma.

Rydych chi eisoes wedi dweud eich bod wedi cyfathrebu â'r Farwnes Longfield ynglŷn â'r ymchwiliadau lleol. Mae hi wedi ateb yr un fath i mi ag y gwnaeth i ohebiaeth gan eraill yn y Siambr hon drwy ddweud y gallai fod ymchwiliadau lleol pellach yn y dyfodol lle mae'r dystiolaeth yn arwain. Rydym eisoes yn gwybod bod problemau wedi bod yng Nghymru, felly mae'r dystiolaeth eisoes yno, ac eto nid ydym wedi gweld unrhyw ymchwiliadau lleol ar hyn o bryd.

Rhaid eich bod yn gweld yr her yn y ddadl rydych chi'n ei chyflwyno nawr o gymharu â'r ddadl a gyflwynwyd gennych pan oedd penderfyniadau'r ymchwiliad COVID yn cael eu gwneud, gan y gwyddom fod problemau diogelu ym maes iechyd, gofal cymdeithasol, tai, ym mhob math o feysydd cymhwysedd datganoledig y mae angen inni sicrhau eu bod yn cael eu harchwilio'n llawn. Dyna pam y carwn eich annog—eich annog o ddifrif—i ystyried eich safbwynt ar hyn, a pheidio â dweud 'Na' yn gyfan gwbl. Hyd yn oed os ydych chi'n dweud, 'Fe wnawn gadw meddwl agored ar hyn', buaswn yn ddiolchgar.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llywydd, I hope you will keep in mind later that I did allow that lengthy intervention, which is, of course, something of fundamental importance here. The nuance here—and nuances are vitally important—is that the COVID inquiry, in terms of the focus of its attention, was going to be on devolved issues. A great deal of the focus here would be something outside of our control, and we want to make sure that this work is centred around not just the experiences of victims at the time, but the experiences of survivors today, and not re-traumatising them by duplicating work, which is why we don't want to—. But again, I fundamentally see the importance, the vital importance, that Wales is fully at the centre of this. It is a point that I will be reinforcing when I meet the Baroness.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Lywydd, rwy'n gobeithio y byddwch chi'n cofio yn nes ymlaen fy mod wedi caniatáu'r ymyriad hir hwnnw, sydd, wrth gwrs, yn rhywbeth hanfodol bwysig yma. Y gwahaniaeth bach yma—ac mae gwahaniaethau bach yn hanfodol bwysig—oedd bod yr ymchwiliad COVID, o ran ei ffocws, yn mynd i fod ar faterion datganoledig. Byddai llawer iawn o'r ffocws yma y tu hwnt i'n rheolaeth, ac rydym am sicrhau bod y gwaith hwn yn canolbwyntio nid yn unig ar brofiadau dioddefwyr ar y pryd, ond ar brofiadau goroeswyr heddiw, ac nid eu haildrawmateiddio drwy ddyblygu gwaith, a dyna pam nad ydym am—. Ond unwaith eto, rwy'n gweld pa mor bwysig, pa mor hanfodol bwysig, yw hi fod Cymru’n gwbl ganolog yn hyn. Mae'n bwynt y byddaf yn ei atgyfnerthu pan fyddaf yn cyfarfod â'r Farwnes.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Os gallaf ffeindio lle'r oeddwn i nawr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, I will repeat, because this bears repetition, if I have already got to this point: child sexual exploitation does not stop at national borders. Understanding the full picture requires evidence to be examined across the range of agencies involved in safeguarding, education, health, policing and criminal justice too. Not all of those are, of course, devolved to us in Wales. What will, what must make children safer is acting on evidence, identifying risks earlier, strengthening safeguarding practice and ensuring that survivors receive the trauma-informed support that they need.

Now, the 'Strategy for Preventing and Responding to Child Sexual Abuse in Wales 2026-2036' explicitly includes action to prevent, identify and respond to group-based sexual exploitation, including grooming gangs. Together with its delivery plan, it sets out a clear ambition that all children in Wales should live free from the harm of child sexual abuse, and that everyone affected by abuse is protected and supported throughout their lives. That is the ambition. We must deliver it, because, collectively, we need to do more and do it better. That is on all of us.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wel, rwy'n ailadrodd, gan fod hyn yn werth ei ailadrodd, os wyf eisoes wedi gwneud y pwynt hwn: nid yw camfanteisio rhywiol ar blant yn gyfyngedig i ffiniau cenedlaethol. I ddeall y darlun llawn, mae angen archwilio tystiolaeth ar draws yr ystod o asiantaethau sy'n ymwneud â diogelu, addysg, iechyd, plismona a chyfiawnder troseddol hefyd. Nid yw pob un o'r rheini wedi'u datganoli i ni yng Nghymru wrth gwrs. Yr hyn a fydd, yr hyn sy'n rhaid iddo wneud plant yn fwy diogel, yw gweithredu ar dystiolaeth, nodi risgiau'n gynharach, cryfhau arferion diogelu a sicrhau bod goroeswyr yn cael y cymorth ystyriol o drawma sydd ei angen arnynt.

Nawr, mae'r 'Strategaeth Genedlaethol ar Atal ac Ymateb i Gam-drin Plant yn Rhywiol yng Nghymru 2026-2036' yn cynnwys camau gweithredu penodol i atal, nodi ac ymateb i gam-drin rhywiol gan grwpiau, gan gynnwys gangiau grŵmio. Ynghyd â'i chynllun cyflawni, mae'n nodi uchelgais glir y dylai pob plentyn yng Nghymru fyw'n rhydd rhag niwed cam-drin plant yn rhywiol, a bod pawb sy'n cael eu cam-drin yn cael eu diogelu a'u cefnogi drwy gydol eu hoes. Dyna'r uchelgais. Rhaid i ni ei gyflawni, oherwydd ar y cyd, mae angen inni wneud mwy a'i wneud yn well. Mae hynny'n ddyletswydd ar bob un ohonom.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Mi fydd angen dull gweithredu system gyfan, gan ddod â gwasanaethau cyhoeddus, partneriaid diogelu, cymunedau a goroeswyr at ei gilydd. Mi fyddwn ni’n rhoi fframwaith hyfforddi cenedlaethol ar waith, yn cryfhau cymorth i ymarferwyr a goroeswyr, ac yn gwella gwasanaethau ledled Cymru.

Ym mis Medi yn unig, daeth mwy na 400 o weithwyr proffesiynol o bob cwr o Gymru a phartneriaid ac arbenigwyr diogelu at ei gilydd i gryfhau gwybodaeth, gwella ymarfer a hybu’r gwaith o weithredu’r strategaeth. Ar ddechrau’r flwyddyn nesaf, mi fydd ymgyrch codi ymwybyddiaeth genedlaethol flynyddol yn cael ei lansio i helpu pobl i adnabod arwyddion o gam-drin a deall y camau y gallan nhw eu cymryd.

Oherwydd mae diogelu yn fusnes i bawb. Er bod plismona a chyfiawnder troseddol yn parhau i fod yn faterion a gedwir yn ôl, rŷn ni’n gweithio’n agos gyda phartneriaid ar draws gwasanaethau cyhoeddus i atal niwed, lleihau troseddu ac adeiladu cymunedau mwy diogel ledled Cymru. Mae’r gwaith hwn hefyd yn cyd-fynd â’n hymrwymiad ehangach i atal trais, cam-drin a chamfanteisio ac i greu cymunedau mwy diogel ledled Cymru.

Mi fyddwn ni’n cyhoeddi strategaeth newydd ar drais yn erbyn menywod, cam-drin domestig a thrais rhywiol yn ystod yr haf flwyddyn nesaf.

Yn gynharach eleni, fe wnes i rannu fy mlaenoriaethau â’r Senedd. Mae cryfhau trefniadau diogelu i amddiffyn plant ac oedolion sy’n wynebu risg yn dal i fod yn un o’m prif flaenoriaethau. Rhaid i leisiau plant fod yn ganolog i benderfyniadau diogelu, gan gynnwys pan fo pryderon yn bodoli ond dyw'r plentyn ddim wedi datgelu hynny’n ffurfiol.

Rydyn ni wedi ymrwymo i gyflwyno dyletswyddau newydd o ran rhoi gwybod am gam-drin plant yn rhywiol, cryfhau safonau diogelu a sicrhau bod gwersi o bryderon diogelu yn arwain at welliant ledled Cymru. Yn ystod yr wythnosau nesaf, bydd yr Aelodau yn cael clywed rhagor am sut rŷn ni’n bwriadu cyflawni’r ymrwymiadau hynny ar lawr y Senedd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
We will need a whole-system approach, bringing public services, safeguarding partners, communities and survivors together. We will implement a national training framework, strengthen support for practitioners and survivors, and improve services across Wales.

In September alone, more than 400 professionals from all over Wales came together with partners and safeguarding experts to strengthen knowledge, improve practice and promote the implementation of the strategy. At the beginning of next year, an annual national awareness campaign will be launched to help people recognise the signs of abuse and to understand the steps that they can take.

Because safeguarding is everyone's business. Although policing and criminal justice remain reserved issues, we work closely with partners across public services to prevent harm, reduce crime and build safer communities across Wales. This work is also in line with our wider commitment to preventing violence, abuse and exploitation and to creating safer communities across Wales.

We will publish a new strategy on violence against women, domestic abuse and sexual violence during the summer of 2027.

Earlier this year, I shared my priorities with the Senedd. Strengthening safeguarding arrangements to protect children and adults who are at risk is still one of my main priorities. Children's voices must be central to safeguarding decisions, including where concerns exist but the child has not formally disclosed that.

We are committed to introducing new duties in terms of reporting child sexual abuse, strengthening safeguarding standards and ensuring that lessons from safeguarding concerns lead to improvements throughout Wales. During the next few weeks, Members will be able to hear more about how we intend to fulfil those commitments on the floor of the Senedd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Llywydd, safeguarding is fundamental to the Wales we want to be. It will continue to be central to this Government's wider ambitions. The Government amendment recognises the seriousness, the terrible seriousness, of these crimes. It recognises that victims and survivors deserve justice and support. It recognises that Wales is within the scope of the statutory inquiry and it commits us—it commits us—to considering carefully any findings and recommendations relating to Wales, and progressing any necessary action.

But importantly, it also focuses on the actions needed to make children safer today. Recent cases we've seen in Wales demonstrate that the responsibility to improve safeguarding, to improve children's lives, begins now. That is why we're strengthening safeguarding arrangements across Wales. That is why safeguarding remains one of my central priorities as Deputy Minister. Because every child deserves to grow up safely. Every victim and survivor deserves to be heard, to be supported, to be treated with dignity. That is the Wales we want, a Wales where children are safer, where abuse is identified earlier, a Wales where survivors receive the support they need throughout their lives, a Wales where survivors receive what they need, where safeguarding arrangements are strong, are effective, are trusted. It is the Wales we must build together, and for those reasons, Llywydd, I ask Members to support the Government amendment.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Lywydd, mae diogelu'n hanfodol i'r Gymru rydym am fod. Bydd yn parhau i fod yn ganolog i uchelgeisiau ehangach y Llywodraeth hon. Mae gwelliant y Llywodraeth yn cydnabod difrifoldeb, difrifoldeb ofnadwy, y troseddau hyn. Mae'n cydnabod bod dioddefwyr a goroeswyr yn haeddu cyfiawnder a chefnogaeth. Mae'n cydnabod bod Cymru o fewn cwmpas yr ymchwiliad statudol ac mae'n ein hymrwymo—yn ein hymrwymo ni—i ystyried yn ofalus unrhyw ganfyddiadau ac argymhellion sy'n gysylltiedig â Chymru, a bwrw ymlaen ag unrhyw gamau angenrheidiol.

Ond yn bwysig, mae hefyd yn canolbwyntio ar y camau gweithredu sydd eu hangen i wneud plant yn fwy diogel heddiw. Mae achosion diweddar a welsom yng Nghymru yn dangos bod y cyfrifoldeb i wella diogelu, i wella bywydau plant, yn dechrau nawr. Dyna pam ein bod yn cryfhau trefniadau diogelu ledled Cymru. Dyna pam y mae diogelu'n parhau i fod yn un o fy mhrif flaenoriaethau fel Dirprwy Weinidog. Oherwydd mae pob plentyn yn haeddu cael tyfu i fyny'n ddiogel. Mae pob dioddefwr a goroeswr yn haeddu cael eu clywed, eu cefnogi, eu trin ag urddas. Dyna'r Gymru rydym ei heisiau, Cymru lle mae plant yn fwy diogel, lle mae cam-drin yn cael ei nodi'n gynharach, Cymru lle mae goroeswyr yn cael y gefnogaeth sydd ei hangen arnynt drwy gydol eu hoes, Cymru lle mae goroeswyr yn cael yr hyn sydd ei angen arnynt, lle mae trefniadau diogelu'n gryf, yn effeithiol, ac yn ennyn hyder. Dyma'r Gymru y mae'n rhaid inni ei hadeiladu gyda'n gilydd, ac am y rhesymau hynny, Lywydd, gofynnaf i'r Aelodau gefnogi gwelliant y Llywodraeth.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. Can I start by thanking all Members who tried to contribute to the spirit of how we hoped today's debate would go? Paul, your bravery inspires us all. What you and your family went through, what you still go through, and to have the courage to walk in this Chamber today and share those experiences, to try to convince Members of the importance of voting for this motion, is a true inspiration to us all. Thank you so much.

Beca Brown, your contribution: I agreed with most of it until the political point-scoring decided to come out, but education is completely right. I agree with you. And there we can find common ground, but that's not enough. There are victims now who've already had these experiences, and what they want is to be heard, to be listened to, and their voices then can turn into action when people like us in this Chamber hear those experiences. There are people today in the gallery and watching this debate at home who are very keen on expressing their experiences in a safe environment, where it's not politicised, where they're listened to, and where action can be delivered. We can't undermine that.

Now, Darren, your motion today—on these benches, we do agree with you that Wales does need its own COVID inquiry, for the points made by several Members today. The reason we didn't include it in this motion is that we thought we could find consensus across the Chamber that there is currently an inquiry, which is called the England and Wales inquiry, which doesn't currently look at anywhere in this nation.

Now, Minister, I understand you said you're going to make the case for it, but I don't understand your amendment today. Can you imagine the power that we could have sent? You could have had a mandate from this very Chamber, uniting us. You would not have been walking in there as a Minister of a minority Government, you'd have walked through that door with a mandate from this Senedd that says, 'Wales should be included.' There should not be a policy here that we're going to learn from what's happening over in England. Is this now the policy of Plaid Cymru?

On Monday, you were sitting with separatists. Today, you're sitting here saying, 'For Wales, see England.' It's not right. Voices must be heard. And those victims have their own experiences—unique. And I'm sure across Wales they're just as unique in different areas. We couldn't pinpoint one area of Wales that has one experience. The contributions from Darren and Tom today, talking about their constituency—experiences there are horrific. But I'm sure it's unique to that area that has a right to be heard, just like Newport—different again. Let's encourage now together. Let's end this amendment. Let's vote together and give you a clear mandate. That's what these victims want, not point scoring. This isn't clickbait. My colleagues on these benches, like Cristiana, wrote herself to the Chair of the committee urging for this to happen; as Darren said, he's done too. We've written to the Home Secretary urging for Wales to be in there. We're looking to give you today the power to walk into that office with a mandate from this Chamber, this Senedd, the elected Members saying, 'Wales must be included.' So, I urge you to think again. Take this opportunity. Take this cross-party consensus. Let's stand up for the victims. Let's not be tribal in this. That's my offer to you today in voting with us for this motion.

It's so shocking that—. I've had letters back from the chair of this inquiry. How on earth can £65 million be allocated under the name of England and Wales and not one county at the moment looked at? Just the offer of 'maybe'—'maybe it could be'. That's unacceptable. Victims and survivors from other inquiries have said how important having their voices in those inquiries were, whether it's COVID, Hillsborough—the list goes on. Inquiries are an important part of recovery, and that's what we must start thinking about. Recovery—I'm glad Members have mentioned it today, and, Minister, I do agree with you—from mental health and physical trauma, and to those victims who have turned to, whether it's substance abuse, we must do better there to support them. And Sarah Rees, your contribution there, it was a really powerful one at the start. I'm sorry it went a little bit tribal then, but I'm glad you raised those issues, and thank you.

There is more that we must do—we know that in this Chamber. And there is a consensus here. So, when we go forward, looking to what's happening here, let's look at the victims, as Paul said, not as statistics, as human beings—someone's daughter or, in some cases, son, someone's child. That is the power of what we have in front of us today. Now, I know it's not legally binding, this motion in the Chamber, but it's a signal we can send, as a united Senedd, saying that victims across Wales will be and must be listened to, that there isn't anyone who can ignore them any longer, and any predator out there will know that this Senedd won't stand for it. Wales won't stand for it.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. A gaf i ddechrau drwy ddiolch i bob Aelod a geisiodd gyfrannu at yr ysbryd roeddem yn gobeithio y byddai'r ddadl heddiw yn cael ei chynnal ynddo? Paul, mae eich dewrder yn ysbrydoliaeth i bawb ohonom. Mae'r hyn yr aethoch chi a'ch teulu drwyddo, yr hyn rydych chi'n dal i fynd drwyddo, a chael y dewrder i gerdded i mewn i'r Siambr hon heddiw a rhannu'r profiadau hynny, i geisio argyhoeddi'r Aelodau o bwysigrwydd pleidleisio o blaid y cynnig hwn, yn ysbrydoliaeth wirioneddol i bob un ohonom. Diolch yn fawr iawn.

Beca Brown, eich cyfraniad chi: roeddwn yn cytuno â'r rhan fwyaf ohono hyd nes y dechreuoch chi geisio sgorio pwyntiau gwleidyddol, ond mae addysg yn sicr yn iawn. Rwy'n cytuno â chi. Ac yno gallwn ddod o hyd i rywfaint o dir cyffredin, ond nid yw hynny'n ddigon. Mae yna ddioddefwyr nawr sydd eisoes wedi cael y profiadau hyn, a'r hyn y maent ei eisiau yw cael eu clywed, i rywun wrando arnynt, ac yna gall eu lleisiau droi'n weithredu pan fydd pobl fel ni yn y Siambr hon yn clywed y profiadau hynny. Mae yna bobl heddiw yn yr oriel ac yn gwylio'r ddadl hon gartref sy'n awyddus iawn i fynegi eu profiadau mewn amgylchedd diogel, lle na chaiff ei gwleidyddoli, lle mae rhywun yn gwrando arnynt, a lle gellir rhoi camau ar waith. Ni allwn danseilio hynny.

Nawr, Darren, eich cynnig chi heddiw—ar y meinciau hyn, rydym yn cytuno â chi fod angen ymchwiliad COVID ei hun ar Gymru, oherwydd y pwyntiau a wnaed gan sawl Aelod heddiw. Y rheswm dros beidio â chynnwys hynny yn y cynnig hwn yw ein bod yn credu y gallem ddod i gonsensws ar draws y Siambr fod ymchwiliad ar y gweill ar hyn o bryd, a elwir yn ymchwiliad Cymru a Lloegr, nad yw'n edrych ar unman yn y genedl hon ar hyn o bryd.

Nawr, Weinidog, rwy'n deall eich bod chi wedi dweud eich bod yn mynd i ddadlau'r achos drosto, ond nid wyf yn deall eich gwelliant heddiw. A allwch chi ddychmygu pŵer y neges y gallem fod wedi'i hanfon? Gallech fod wedi cael mandad gan y Siambr hon, yn ein huno. Ni fyddech wedi bod yn cerdded i mewn yno fel Gweinidog Llywodraeth leiafrifol, byddech wedi cerdded drwy'r drws gyda mandad gan y Senedd hon sy'n dweud, 'Dylid cynnwys Cymru.' Ni ddylai fod polisi yma y byddwn yn dysgu o'r hyn sy'n digwydd yn Lloegr. Ai dyma bolisi Plaid Cymru nawr?

Ddydd Llun, roeddech chi'n eistedd gydag ymwahanwyr. Heddiw, rydych chi'n eistedd yma'n dweud, 'Ar gyfer Cymru, gweler Lloegr.' Nid yw hynny'n iawn. Rhaid i leisiau gael eu clywed. Ac mae gan y dioddefwyr hynny eu profiadau eu hunain—unigryw. Ac rwy'n siŵr eu bod yr un mor unigryw mewn gwahanol ardaloedd. Ni allem nodi un ardal o Gymru sydd â'r un profiad. Mae cyfraniadau Darren a Tom heddiw, yn siarad am eu hetholaeth—mae'r profiadau yno'n erchyll. Ond rwy'n siŵr eu bod yn unigryw i'r ardal honno sydd â hawl i gael ei chlywed, yn union fel Casnewydd—sy'n wahanol eto. Gadewch inni annog nawr gyda'n gilydd. Gadewch inni roi diwedd ar y gwelliant hwn. Gadewch inni bleidleisio gyda'n gilydd a rhoi mandad clir i chi. Dyna mae'r dioddefwyr hyn ei eisiau, nid sgorio pwyntiau. Nid abwyd clicio mohono. Ysgrifennodd fy nghyd-Aelodau ar y meinciau hyn, fel Cristiana, at Gadeirydd y pwyllgor yn annog hyn; fel y dywedodd Darren, mae yntau wedi gwneud hynny hefyd. Rydym wedi ysgrifennu at yr Ysgrifennydd Cartref yn eu hannog i gynnwys Cymru. Ein bwriad yw rhoi'r pŵer heddiw i chi gerdded i mewn i'r swyddfa honno gyda mandad gan y Siambr hon, y Senedd hon, yr Aelodau etholedig, yn dweud, 'Rhaid cynnwys Cymru.' Felly, rwy'n eich annog i feddwl eto. Manteisiwch ar y cyfle hwn. Manteisiwch ar y consensws trawsbleidiol. Gadewch inni sefyll o blaid y dioddefwyr. Gadewch inni beidio â bod yn blwyfol yn hyn. Dyna fy nghynnig i chi heddiw wrth bleidleisio gyda ni dros y cynnig hwn.

Mae mor syfrdanol fod—. Rwyf wedi cael llythyrau yn ôl gan gadeirydd yr ymchwiliad hwn. Sut ar y ddaear y gellir dyrannu £65 miliwn o dan enw Cymru a Lloegr heb ystyried yr un sir ar hyn o bryd? Dim ond cynnig 'efallai'—'efallai y gallai fod'. Mae hynny'n annerbyniol. Mae dioddefwyr a goroeswyr o ymchwiliadau eraill wedi dweud pa mor bwysig oedd cael eu lleisiau yn yr ymchwiliadau hynny, boed yn COVID, Hillsborough—mae'r rhestr yn parhau. Mae ymchwiliadau'n rhan bwysig o adferiad, a dyna sy'n rhaid inni ddechrau meddwl amdano. Adferiad—rwy'n falch fod yr Aelodau wedi sôn am hynny heddiw, ac rwy'n cytuno â chi, Weinidog—o iechyd meddwl a thrawma corfforol, ac i'r dioddefwyr hynny sydd wedi troi at, boed yn gamddefnyddio sylweddau, mae’n rhaid inni wneud yn well yno i'w cefnogi. A Sarah Rees, eich cyfraniad yno, roedd yn un pwerus iawn ar y dechrau. Mae’n ddrwg gennyf fod pethau wedi mynd braidd yn blwyfol wedyn, ond rwy'n falch eich bod wedi codi'r materion hynny, a diolch.

Mae mwy y mae'n rhaid inni ei wneud—fe wyddom hynny yn y Siambr. Ac mae consensws yma. Felly, pan fyddwn yn bwrw ymlaen, ac yn edrych ar yr hyn sy'n digwydd yma, gadewch inni edrych ar y dioddefwyr, fel y dywedodd Paul, nid fel ystadegau, ond fel bodau dynol—merch rhywun, neu mewn rhai achosion, mab, plentyn rhywun. Dyna bŵer yr hyn sydd o'n blaenau heddiw. Nawr, fe wn nad yw'n gyfreithiol rwymol, y cynnig hwn yn y Siambr, ond mae'n neges y gallwn ei hanfon, fel Senedd unedig, i ddweud y bydd dioddefwyr ledled Cymru’n cael eu clywed a bod yn rhaid gwrando arnynt, nad oes unrhyw un a all eu hanwybyddu mwyach, a bydd unrhyw dramgwyddwr allan yno'n gwybod na fydd y Senedd hon yn ei oddef. Ni fydd Cymru’n ei oddef.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Dadl Reform UK: Gangiau grŵmio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Reform UK Debate: Grooming gangs
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
The £65 million is allocated by the UK Government. It's a strange scenario; the finance Minister here should be quite happy that Reform isn't asking her to spend any money from the Welsh budget today. We must be included in there, and I hope, when you do meet the chair of the inquiry and other members, that the case is made clearly. And we need to do it without anything else but seeking truth. I don't want anything else—slurs or racism or anything else. All I want in this—and where I agree with the Chair of the committee—is to follow the evidence. Let's empower the police to do what they must do. But we will be voting with the Conservatives on their amendment today, because I believe that there are other cases that we need to get to the bottom of in Wales, whichever layer of body that is.

Cristiana raised several points there that I think should be listened to, and she's raised this passionately time and time again. I hope, when we do leave this Chamber today, we can say that victims will not be ignored. I've heard it across the Chamber, but that isn't enough, us standing here saying it—me standing here saying it isn't. How we vote tonight is what matters. Action from this is what matters.

I heard a powerful story before this debate was tabled, by someone I'm going to call Jane. She's a survivor herself. She was ignored when she talked about her experiences. She was used as what she described as a sexual object, not a human being. From her experience, from what they were doing when they were drugging her—that addiction continued after. The way society labelled her, and what she was—as a drug addict, and a slur, Llywydd, that I will not say in the Chamber, but Members can imagine. Today she has found her way to speak out, to work for a charity helping other people. Her experience has helped more and more young women, women who have come to terms with being able to speak out, to come to terms with what happened and begin their recovery process. And she's watching now and I would like it on the record, which is why I'm saying it, her bravery and actions, and how she's turned a horrific, horrific crime that was made against her, into a positive and a better way of society should inspire us all. For me, it encouraged me to speak out today in this Chamber. And that's the power of speaking out. That's the power of one person speaking to me, to inspire me to speak out in this Chamber today. By letting those victims or survivors—however they wish to be referred to—into that inquiry to be heard is vital. It could inspire another generation, it could open up a lot of eyes into ways we've never considered, or maybe we've walked past blindly.

So, I urge Members, in closing today, to consider what the motion in front of them is. We're not trying to point score. We're not trying to politicise something. We have taken real experiences, listened to real voices and we're urging you today to send a clear signal to the chair of the inquiry: let Wales in. And if you vote to silence us today on that, we will be back, because these voices must be heard. Diolch yn fawr, Lywydd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae'r £65 miliwn wedi'i ddyrannu gan Lywodraeth y DU. Mae'n senario ryfedd; dylai'r Gweinidog cyllid yma fod yn falch nad yw Reform yn gofyn iddi wario unrhyw arian o gyllideb Cymru heddiw. Rhaid ein cynnwys yno, a gobeithio, pan fyddwch yn cyfarfod â chadeirydd yr ymchwiliad ac aelodau eraill, y bydd yr achos yn cael ei ddadlau'n glir. Ac mae angen inni wneud hynny heb unrhyw beth arall heblaw ceisio'r gwirionedd. Nid wyf eisiau unrhyw beth arall—sarhad na hiliaeth nac unrhyw beth arall. Y cyfan rwyf ei eisiau yn hyn—a lle rwy'n cytuno â Chadeirydd y pwyllgor—yw dilyn y dystiolaeth. Gadewch inni rymuso'r heddlu i wneud yr hyn y mae'n rhaid iddynt ei wneud. Ond byddwn yn pleidleisio gyda'r Ceidwadwyr ar eu gwelliant heddiw, gan y credaf fod achosion eraill y mae angen inni fynd at eu gwraidd yng Nghymru, ar ba lefel bynnag.

Cododd Cristiana sawl pwynt yno y credaf y dylid gwrando arnynt, ac mae wedi codi hyn yn angerddol dro ar ôl tro. Pan fyddwn yn gadael y Siambr hon heddiw, rwy'n gobeithio y gallwn ddweud na fydd dioddefwyr yn cael eu hanwybyddu. Rwyf wedi clywed hynny ar draws y Siambr, ond nid yw'n ddigon ein bod ni'n sefyll yma'n ei ddweud—nid yw i mi sefyll yma'n ei ddweud yn ddigon. Sut rydym yn pleidleisio heno yw'r hyn sy'n bwysig. Gweithredu ar hyn sy'n bwysig.

Clywais stori bwerus cyn i'r ddadl hon gael ei chyflwyno, gan rywun rwy'n mynd i'w galw'n Jane. Mae hi'n oroeswr ei hun. Cafodd ei hanwybyddu pan siaradodd am ei phrofiadau. Cafodd ei defnyddio fel yr hyn a ddisgrifiodd fel gwrthrych rhywiol, nid bod dynol. O'i phrofiad hi, o'r hyn roeddent yn ei wneud pan oeddent yn rhoi cyffuriau iddi—parhaodd y ddibyniaeth honno ar ôl hynny. Y ffordd y gwnaeth cymdeithas ei labelu hi, a'r hyn oedd hi—fel rhywun a oedd yn gaeth i gyffuriau, a gair nad wyf am ei ddweud yn y Siambr, Lywydd, ond gall yr Aelodau ddychmygu. Heddiw, mae hi wedi dod o hyd i ffordd o godi ei llais, i weithio i elusen sy'n helpu pobl eraill. Mae ei phrofiad wedi helpu mwy a mwy o fenywod ifanc, menywod sydd wedi dod i delerau â gallu codi eu llais, i delerau â'r hyn a ddigwyddodd, a dechrau ar eu hadferiad. Ac mae hi'n gwylio nawr, a hoffwn gofnodi, a dyna pam rwy'n dweud hyn, ei dewrder a'i gweithredoedd, a dylai'r ffordd y mae hi wedi troi trosedd gwbl erchyll yn ei herbyn yn rhywbeth cadarnhaol ac yn ffordd well o ymdrin â chymdeithas ysbrydoli pob un ohonom. I mi, fe wnaeth fy annog i siarad heddiw yn y Siambr hon. A dyna bŵer codi eich llais. Dyna bŵer un unigolyn yn siarad â mi, i fy ysbrydoli i godi fy llais yn y Siambr hon heddiw. Mae gadael i'r dioddefwyr neu'r goroeswyr hynny—sut bynnag y maent yn dymuno cael eu galw—gael eu clywed yn yr ymchwiliad hwnnw yn hanfodol. Gallai ysbrydoli cenhedlaeth arall, gallai agor llawer o lygaid i ffyrdd nad ydym erioed wedi'u hystyried, neu efallai ein bod wedi cerdded heibio iddynt yn ddall.

Felly, wrth gloi heddiw, rwy'n annog yr Aelodau i ystyried beth yw'r cynnig o'u blaenau. Nid ydym yn ceisio sgorio pwyntiau. Nid ydym yn ceisio gwleidyddoli rhywbeth. Rydym wedi cymryd profiadau go iawn, wedi gwrando ar leisiau go iawn ac rydym yn eich annog chi heddiw i anfon neges glir at gadeirydd yr ymchwiliad: gadewch i Gymru gael ei chynnwys. Ac os byddwch chi'n pleidleisio i'n tawelu ar hynny heddiw, byddwn yn ôl, gan fod yn rhaid i'r lleisiau hyn gael eu clywed. Diolch yn fawr, Lywydd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Reform UK Debate: Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board health visitor pay dispute
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Cynnig NDM9294 Llŷr Powell

Cefnogwyd gan Andrew Griffin, Cristiana Emsley, John Clark, Sarah Cooper-Lesadd

Cynnig bod y Senedd:

1. Yn gresynu at yr anghydfod cyflog parhaus rhwng ymwelwyr iechyd yng Nghymru a Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Cwm Taf Morgannwg.

2. Yn galw ar Lywodraeth Cymru i gymryd camau ar unwaith i hwyluso datrysiad boddhaol i'r anghydfod, gan gynnwys cynnig cyflog teg, ac i roi terfyn ar y streic.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Motion NDM9294 Llŷr Powell

Supported by Andrew Griffin, Cristiana Emsley, John Clark, Sarah Cooper-Lesadd

To propose that the Senedd:

1. Regrets the ongoing pay dispute between Welsh health visitors and Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board.

2. Calls on the Welsh Government to take immediate action to facilitate a satisfactory resolution to the dispute, including a fair pay offer, and to bring an end to strike action.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl Reform UK: Anghydfod cyflogau ymwelwyr iechyd Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Cwm Taf Morgannwg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Reform UK Debate: Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board health visitor pay dispute
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. I stand today in favour of the Reform motion. Between March and May of last year, Cwm Taf Morgannwg carried out 6,410 health visitor visits. In the same three months this year, there were just 909. That isn't a minor adjustment, it's a complete collapse. Babies are missing their checks, safeguarding referrals are a fraction of last year's levels and charities supporting new mothers say that demand has at least doubled for these services, if not trebled. Children in some of the poorest communities in Wales are paying for a dispute that should have been resolved months ago.

And Plaid Cymru know this. I have in my hand today, Llywydd, a letter signed by the current First Minister. He signed it during the election campaign in April. In this letter, he said that the failure to reach a fair settlement was unacceptable, and he called for immediate action for band 6 health visitors to be upgraded to band 7. In March, the current Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport said that all health visitors should be band 7, not band 6, and that an all-female workforce were being denied the pay that they deserved.

Now, those were warm words from Plaid Cymru in opposition, but that was before they had the power to resolve this issue. Now they do. So what has the party done to solve the problem? The health Minister told this Chamber that the industrial action is a dispute between the health board and Unite that relates to decisions over several years. The Welsh Government has said that this is a regrettable situation that should not have occurred in the first place—quite the change in tone from the immediate action that they urged prior to the election.

Health visitors who voted for Plaid Cymru are now asking if the pre-election assurances they were given were misguided or simply false. I have in my hand, Llywydd, another letter, this one written by Unite the Union. In it, they say:

'Many of us voted and campaigned for Plaid, and placed trust in promises you made that a new approach would be taken to resolve this dispute.

'At best were you reckless with your promises or is the question "Has Plaid Lied?"'

Now, that's not my question. Those are the words of health visitors who are being let down by this Plaid Cymru Government.

Asking both sides to come back to the table is not action; it is an abdication. The Welsh Government needs to take immediate action to resolve this dispute, including a fair pay offer to bring an end to strike action. Rhun ap Iorwerth said in April that the failure to settle this dispute was unacceptable. Those words were true then and they are true now. The difference is that now Plaid Cymru have the power to solve this dispute. So, I urge them to use that power and do so. Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. Rwy'n codi heddiw i gefnogi cynnig Reform. Rhwng mis Mawrth a mis Mai y llynedd, cyflawnodd Cwm Taf Morgannwg 6,410 o ymweliadau gan ymwelwyr iechyd. Yn yr un tri mis eleni, dim ond 909 a wnaed. Nid yw hynny'n addasiad bach, mae'n chwalfa lwyr. Mae babanod yn colli archwiliadau, mae atgyfeiriadau diogelu ar lefel lawer is na'r llynedd ac mae elusennau sy'n cefnogi mamau newydd yn dweud bod y galw am y gwasanaethau hyn wedi dyblu, os nad treblu. Mae plant yn rhai o'r cymunedau tlotaf yng Nghymru yn talu am anghydfod y dylid bod wedi ei ddatrys fisoedd yn ôl.

Ac mae Plaid Cymru yn gwybod hyn. Lywydd, yn fy llaw mae gennyf lythyr wedi'i lofnodi gan y Prif Weinidog presennol. Fe'i llofnododd yn ystod yr ymgyrch etholiadol ym mis Ebrill. Yn y llythyr hwn, dywedodd fod y methiant i ddod i gytundeb teg yn annerbyniol, a galwodd am weithredu ar unwaith i ymwelwyr iechyd band 6 gael eu huwchraddio i fand 7. Ym mis Mawrth, dywedodd y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon y dylai pob ymwelydd iechyd fod ym mand 7, nid band 6, a bod gweithlu benywaidd yn cael eu hamddifadu o'r cyflog yr oeddent yn ei haeddu.

Nawr, geiriau cynnes gan Blaid Cymru pan oedd yn wrthblaid oedd y rheini, ond roedd hynny cyn iddynt gael pŵer i ddatrys y mater. Mae ganddynt y pŵer hwnnw nawr. Felly beth y mae'r blaid wedi'i wneud i ddatrys y broblem? Dywedodd y Gweinidog iechyd wrth y Siambr hon fod y gweithredu diwydiannol yn anghydfod rhwng y bwrdd iechyd ac Unite sy'n ymwneud â phenderfyniadau dros sawl blwyddyn. Mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi dweud bod hon yn sefyllfa anffodus na ddylai fod wedi digwydd yn y lle cyntaf—cryn dipyn o newid cywair o'r gweithredu uniongyrchol yr oeddent yn ei annog cyn yr etholiad.

Mae ymwelwyr iechyd a bleidleisiodd dros Blaid Cymru bellach yn gofyn a oedd y sicrwydd a roddwyd iddynt cyn yr etholiad yn gamarweiniol neu'n ffug. Mae gennyf lythyr arall yn fy llaw, Lywydd, yr un hwn wedi'i ysgrifennu gan undeb Unite. Ynddo, maent yn dweud:

'Fe wnaeth llawer ohonom bleidleisio ac ymgyrchu dros Blaid Cymru, ac ymddiried yn yr addewidion a wnaethoch y byddai dull newydd o weithredu'n cael ei arfer i ddatrys yr anghydfod hwn.

'Ar y gorau, a oeddech chi'n ddi-hid gyda'ch addewidion neu ai'r cwestiwn yw "A yw Plaid Cymru wedi dweud celwydd?"'

Nawr, nid fy nghwestiwn i yw hwnnw. Dyna eiriau ymwelwyr iechyd sy'n cael eu siomi gan Lywodraeth Plaid Cymru.

Nid gweithredu yw gofyn i'r ddwy ochr ddod yn ôl at y bwrdd; mae'n droi cefn. Mae angen i Lywodraeth Cymru roi camau ar waith ar unwaith i ddatrys yr anghydfod hwn, gan gynnwys cynnig cyflog teg i ddod â'r streic i ben. Dywedodd Rhun ap Iorwerth ym mis Ebrill fod y methiant i ddatrys yr anghydfod hwn yn annerbyniol. Roedd y geiriau hynny'n wir bryd hynny ac maent yn wir nawr. Y gwahaniaeth yw bod gan Blaid Cymru bŵer i ddatrys yr anghydfod hwn. Felly, rwy'n eu hannog i ddefnyddio'r pŵer hwnnw a gwneud hynny. Diolch yn fawr.

Gwelliant 2—Heledd Fychan

Dileu popeth ar ôl pwynt 1 a rhoi yn ei le:

Yn cydnabod bod y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal wedi annog Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Cwm Taf Morgannwg ac Unite dro ar ôl tro i ddod ynghyd i ddatrys yr anghydfod hwn er mwyn lleihau'r effaith ar fabanod, teuluoedd a staff, a'i fod yn parhau'n ymrwymedig i hyrwyddo gweithio mewn partneriaeth gadarnhaol ar bob lefel ac i ddatrys anghydfodau lleol drwy drafod cyn gynted â phosibl.

Yn cydnabod bod Llywodraeth Cymru wedi ymrwymo i sicrhau gweithlu ymwelwyr iechyd diogel a sefydlog ledled Cymru, a bod Prif Swyddog Nyrsio Cymru wedi comisiynu gwaith i adolygu ac ystyried y ffordd y darperir gwasanaethau ymwelwyr iechyd yn y dyfodol er mwyn sicrhau bod y model yn parhau i ddiwallu anghenion plant, teuluoedd a chymunedau.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Amendment 2—Heledd Fychan

Delete all after point 1 and replace with:

Acknowledges that the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care has repeatedly urged Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board and Unite to come together and resolve this dispute to minimise the impact on babies, families, and staff and remains committed to encouraging positive partnership working at every level and the resolution of local dispute through negotiation as soon as possible.

Recognises that the Welsh Government is committed to a secure and stable health visiting workforce across Wales and that the Chief Nursing Officer for Wales has commissioned work to review and consider the future delivery of health visiting services to ensure that the model continues to meet the needs of children, families, and communities.
